cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Vendors page from the left navigation panel. 2. Navigate to the Prospects Tab. 3. Select the vendor to onboard. 4. Click the blue "Start Onboarding" button. 5. In the "Onboarding Prospects" side panel, select a template under "Onboarding Template". 6. Confirm to send the prospect to the onboarding event.
cases.expected: Onboarding starts for the prospect, who moves to the "Onboarding in Progress" tab.
cases.oracle: Prospect listed under "Onboarding in Progress"; success state "You have successfully started the onboarding for a vendor!".

cases.section: How do I Start Onboarding a Vendor?
cases.title: Prospects tab lists invited but not onboarded vendors
cases.why: Prospects are defined as vendors invited but not onboarded yet.
cases.setup: Onboarding enabled; one vendor invited and not onboarded, one vendor Joined.
cases.steps: 1. Open the Vendors page and the Prospects tab.
cases.expected: The invited, not-yet-onboarded vendor is listed; the Joined vendor is not.
cases.oracle: Prospects tab contents match the two vendors' states.

cases.section: How do I Start Onboarding a Vendor?
cases.title: View vendor responses on the Onboarding Details tab
cases.why: The buyer reviews submitted onboarding responses here.

cases.expected: The Vendor Profile Page opens; Onboarding Details shows the vendor's responses once submitted.

cases.section: How does a Vendor register and log in for the first time?
cases.title: First-time vendor sign-in with email OTP and sign-up

On the **Vendor Sign up** page, review the pre-filled details. 5. Click the checkbox next to "I agree to the terms of use,…". 6. Click the blue "Submit" button.
cases.expected: The Vendor Sign up page shows details pre-filled by the inviting buyer; after Submit the vendor is logged into the platform.

cases.section: How does a Vendor register and log in for the first time?

cases.title: Bulk upload vendors from the Excel template

cases.title: Section scores are auto-summed

cases.title: Vendor Approval Levels (vendor.approval.levels) = 2 (default)
cases.why: Different organizations have different governance requirements. A startup may need 1 approver; an enterprise like JSPL needs Finance + Legal + Category approval.
cases.setup: Persona: Tenant Admin and Buyer. Plan: any tenant (Plan Required: All Plans). gate: `vendor.approval.levels` = 2 (default: 2) — CONF-VM-003 "Vendor Approval Levels", Number, risk if changed: High.
cases.steps: 1. As the Tenant Admin, set `vendor.approval.levels` to 2. 2. As a Buyer: use Buyer-Initiated Vendor Invitation to invite a new supplier with their primary details into the Prospect list. 3. Observe the behaviour the setting controls: number of sequential approval levels required before a vendor is activated.
cases.expected: The value 2 is accepted and takes effect. What the setting controls: Number of sequential approval levels required before a vendor is activated. Stated business impact: Directly affects how many people must approve each new vendor; reducing this relaxes controls, increasing it adds friction.
cases.oracle: The behaviour in step 3 reflects the value 2 exactly (the boundary of 1 – 5 is honoured).

cases.title: Buyer-Initiated Vendor Invitation: refused for a user without the Buyer role

cases.title: VMS / VRP Import: not available on the Growth plan
cases.why: The workbook limits VMS / VRP Import to "Enterprise". A tenant on a lower plan must not get it, or plan packaging is not enforced.
cases.setup: Persona: Implementation Partner. Plan: tenant on the Growth plan (Plan Required: Enterprise). Status: GA.
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as an Implementation Partner on the lower-plan tenant. 2. Try it: use VMS / VRP Import to import vendors directly from the enterprise's existing VMS/VRP. 3. Repeat on a tenant on Enterprise.
cases.expected: On the Growth plan the capability is not available to use. On Enterprise the same steps work.
cases.oracle: Same user role, same steps, different plan: refused or absent on the lower plan, available on Enterprise.

cases.title: VMS / VRP Import: refused for a user without the Implementation Partner role
cases.why: The workbook names Implementation Partner as the user of VMS / VRP Import. If any role can do it, the intended separation of duties is gone.
cases.setup: Persona: a user who holds none of these roles: Implementation Partner. Plan: tenant on Enterprise (lowest plan with access; Plan Required: Enterprise). Status: GA.
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as that user on the tenant described in Setup. 2. Try it: use VMS / VRP Import to import vendors directly from the enterprise's existing VMS/VRP. 3. Repeat as an Implementation Partner.
cases.expected: The user without the role cannot carry out the action — Procol refuses it or does not offer it — while the Implementation Partner can. (If the tenant's RBAC deliberately grants it to more roles, record that configuration rather than a defect.)
cases.oracle: Same tenant, same steps, different role: refused or absent for the other user, available to the Implementation Partner.

cases.oracle: The behaviour observed in step 2 and step 3 differs exactly as the two configured values dictate; identical behaviour under different settings means the setting is ignored.

cases.oracle: Tax ID field label changes with the country selection.

cases.section: How do I start processing my PRs
cases.title: Process PR line items through the Purchase Cart into a Sourcing Project
cases.why: This is the entry of the core path from requisition to sourcing event: selected PR lines become a Sourcing Project with events.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page; one or more Open PR line items.
cases.steps: 1. Select the checkbox next to each PR line item to process (multiple allowed). 2. Click the blue "🛒 Purchase Items" button on the top right. 3. In the side panel, review the selected items and their quantities. 4. Click the blue "Create Project" button on the bottom right. 5. Select which events to create as part of the Sourcing Project. 6. Click "Create Project" again.
cases.expected: A side panel lists the selected items with quantities, and after the second "Create Project" the user proceeds to setting up the chosen events.
cases.oracle: The event set-up screen opens for the new Sourcing Project containing the selected line items.

cases.title: Raise a "New Activity" purchase intake request and trigger its approval workflow
cases.why: The Purchase Intake Request is how end users start a purchase without email; submitting it must trigger the approval workflow that later creates the Purchase Request.
cases.setup: End user / requestor (e.g. departmental, operations, admin or planning team member) with access to the Intake page; at least one product in the catalogue and a delivery location.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the "Intake" page from the left-side navigation panel. 2. Click "Create Request". 3. On the Create Intake Request page, enter a Request Title. 4. Select the Request Condition "New Activity". 5. Click "Next" to the Basic Details section, then "Next" to the Details Page. 6. Select the Currency and fill any custom fields shown. 7. In Product Details, search and select the Product Name, enter Quantity, choose the Unit of Measure and select the Delivery Location. 8. Click "Next" to view the Approval Workflow; review and confirm the approval chain. 9. Click "Next" to submit the intake.
cases.expected: The intake is submitted and the approval workflow is triggered.
cases.oracle: The submitted intake shows its approval workflow (approval chain) as started.

cases.title: Approval chain is auto-assigned on the Approval Workflow step
cases.why: Requestors do not pick approvers; the chain is determined by category, department or configuration, and must be visible before submission.
cases.setup: Requestor mid-way through an intake request with product details filled.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Next" from the Details Page to reach the Approval Workflow. 2. Review the approval chain shown.
cases.expected: The Approval Workflow is auto-determined based on category, department or configuration, and the system automatically assigns the approval chain based on the selected categories or item details.
cases.oracle: The Approval Workflow step shows a pre-filled approval chain the requestor did not enter.

cases.title: Approved purchase intake automatically generates a Purchase Request
cases.why: The whole value of the intake flow is that approval produces a Purchase Request with no manual procurement step.
cases.setup: A submitted purchase intake request; access to its approver(s).
cases.steps: 1. Submit a purchase intake request (as in PRD-KBPTP-001). 2. Have the approver(s) in its workflow approve it.
cases.expected: Once approved, the system automatically generates a Purchase Request, enabling procurement to proceed in Procol.
cases.oracle: A Purchase Request exists for the approved intake.

cases.section: How to Approve and Complete an Intake Request
cases.title: Submitted intake shows a visual approval flowchart with creator, current approver and levels
cases.why: The flowchart is the audit view of who must approve and in what order.
cases.setup: An intake request just submitted whose workflow has more than one approval level; approver or requestor logged in.
cases.steps: 1. Open the submitted intake request. 2. Look at the approval workflow.
cases.expected: An approval workflow was triggered automatically, and a visual flowchart shows the name of the user who created the intake, the current approver(s), and each approval level in sequential order.
cases.oracle: The flowchart lists the creator, the current approver(s) and the levels in order.

cases.section: How to Approve and Complete an Intake Request
cases.title: Approver approves an intake with remarks; workflow and Comments tab update
cases.why: Each approval must be recorded with who and when, and remarks must be preserved.
cases.setup: Approver (department head, budget owner or procurement lead) who is the current approver of a submitted intake request.
cases.steps: 1. Open the intake request. 2. Enter a remark in the Remarks / Comments field. 3. Click Approve.
cases.expected: The workflow updates in real time to show who approved and the timestamp; the remark is visible in the Comments tab on the right.
cases.oracle: The flowchart shows the approver's name and timestamp against their level; the Comments tab shows the remark.

cases.section: How to Approve and Complete an Intake Request
cases.title: Approver rejects an intake; workflow records who rejected and when
cases.why: Rejection is the control half of the approval; it must be recorded as clearly as an approval.
cases.setup: Approver who is the current approver of a submitted intake request.
cases.steps: 1. Open the intake request. 2. Enter a remark explaining the rejection. 3. Click Reject.
cases.expected: The workflow updates in real time to show who rejected and the timestamp; the remark appears in the Comments tab.
cases.oracle: The flowchart shows the rejection with approver name and timestamp; the Comments tab shows the remark.

cases.section: How to Approve and Complete an Intake Request
cases.title: Multi-level intake approval proceeds level by level in sequence
cases.why: Sequential levels mean a later approver should act only after the earlier level; order is a compliance control.
cases.setup: Submitted intake whose workflow has at least two approval levels; both approvers available.
cases.steps: 1. As the level-1 approver, approve the intake. 2. Check the flowchart for the current approver. 3. As the level-2 approver, approve the intake.
cases.expected: The levels appear in sequential order and the workflow moves from level 1 to level 2 as each approves.
cases.oracle: After level 1 approves, the flowchart shows level 2 as the current approver; both approvals carry timestamps in order.

cases.section: How to Approve and Complete an Intake Request
cases.title: All approvals complete: Purchase Request generated and linked on the workflow chart
cases.why: This is the hand-off from intake to procurement; the PR must be created and reachable from the intake.
cases.setup: An intake created to initiate a Purchase Request, with all but the last approval done; last approver logged in.
cases.steps: 1. As the last approver, approve the intake. 2. Wait a few minutes and reopen the intake's workflow chart. 3. Click the Purchase Request hyperlink on the workflow chart.
cases.expected: The system automatically generates a Purchase Request within minutes; a hyperlink to it appears on the workflow chart; clicking it opens the Purchase Request detail page directly.
cases.oracle: The workflow chart shows the PR hyperlink and it opens the Purchase Request detail page.

cases.section: How to Approve and Complete an Intake Request
cases.title: Fully approved intake is complete and closed
cases.why: A completed intake must leave the approval queue; a lingering open intake could be acted on twice.
cases.setup: An intake that has received all approvals and generated its Purchase Request.
cases.steps: 1. Open the intake request after the final approval.
cases.expected: The intake request is considered complete and closed in the system.
cases.oracle: The intake shows as complete/closed and no further approval action is pending on it.

cases.section: How to Raise a Purchase Intake Request
cases.title: Raise a purchase intake request (article flow) and submit it for approval
cases.why: This article is the main written procedure for purchase intakes; once approved it must yield a Purchase Request.
cases.setup: End user / requestor with access to the Intake page. Note: the article as written selects Request Condition "Material Creation" with Category and Subcategory, then fills Product Details.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the "Intake" page from the left-side navigation panel and click "Create Request". 2. Enter a Request Title. 3. Select the Request Condition "Material Creation"; choose Category and Subcategory from the dropdowns that appear. 4. Click "Next" to the Basic Details section, then "Next" to the Details Page. 5. Select the Currency and fill any custom fields. 6. In Product Details, select the Product Name, enter Quantity, choose the Unit of Measure and select the Delivery Location. 7. Click "Next" to the Approval Workflow; review and confirm the auto-assigned approval chain. 8. Click "Next" to submit.
cases.expected: The intake is submitted and the approval workflow is triggered; once approved, the system automatically generates a Purchase Request.
cases.oracle: The intake shows its approval workflow started; after approval a Purchase Request exists for it.

cases.section: How to Raise a Material Creation Request via Intake
cases.title: Raise a Material Creation intake request and trigger its approval workflow
cases.why: New materials enter the material master through this approved intake; submission must start the approval.
cases.setup: Requestor / end user (operations or planning) with access to the Intake page.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the "Intake" page and click "Create Request". 2. Enter a Request Title (e.g. "Add New Raw Material - HDPE Granules"). 3. Select the Request Condition "Material Creation". 4. Click "Next" to the Basic Details section. 5. Fill Item Description, Item Type, Unit of Measure, Category and Subcategory (Material Code optional). 6. Click "Next" to review the Approval Workflow; review and confirm the auto-assigned approval chain. 7. Click "Next" to submit.
cases.expected: The intake is submitted and the approval workflow is triggered.
cases.oracle: The submitted intake shows its approval workflow started.

cases.section: How to Raise a Material Creation Request via Intake
cases.title: Approved Material Creation request results in the material being added to the system
cases.why: The request is only useful if approval leads to the material existing in the master.
cases.setup: A submitted Material Creation intake; its approver(s); access to the material master.
cases.steps: 1. Have all approvers in the workflow approve the intake. 2. Check the material master after the relevant team / integration has processed it.
cases.expected: Upon approval, the material is added to the system by the relevant team or system integration process.
cases.oracle: The requested material is present in the material master.

cases.section: How to Create Budgets and Manage Budgets
cases.title: Create a department budget with categories and submit it for approval
cases.why: Budgets cap departmental spend; creation must end in an Approval Note routed through the approval workflow.
cases.setup: Budget owner with access to Budget Management; a department, period type and fiscal year range to budget for; participant teams available.
cases.steps: 1. On Budget Management, click "+ New". 2. On the Budget Creation page, fill Department Name, Period Type and Fiscal Year Range. 3. Assign participant teams from the dropdown lists. 4. In the Budget Category List tab, click "+ New" and fill Category Name, Budget Allocated and Budget Spent. 5. Click "Submit Budget". 6. Review the Approval Workflow preview and click "Submit".
cases.expected: An Approval Note is generated showing the budget details and approval workflow; once approved the budget is created.
cases.oracle: The Approval Note exists with the budget details and workflow; the budget appears in the Budget Department List.

cases.section: How to Create Budgets and Manage Budgets
cases.title: Budget category Balance Amount is auto-calculated as Allocated minus Spent
cases.why: Balance is the money figure every later spend check relies on; a wrong balance lets spend exceed the budget.
cases.setup: Budget owner on the Budget Creation page, Budget Category List tab.
cases.steps: 1. Click "+ New" under the Budget Category List tab. 2. Enter a Category Name, Budget Allocated 100000 and Budget Spent 25000.
cases.expected: The Balance Amount is auto-calculated as Allocated − Spent.
cases.oracle: The Balance Amount shows 75000 without being typed.

cases.section: How to Create Budgets and Manage Budgets
cases.title: Budget-level Allocated, Spent and Balance are system-calculated, not user-entered
cases.why: Header money totals must come from the system; user-entered totals could disagree with the category figures.
cases.setup: Budget owner on the Budget Creation page.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Show More". 2. Inspect the Allocated Budget, Spent Budget and Balance Amount fields. 3. Add budget categories with allocated and spent amounts.
cases.expected: These fields are automatically calculated based on later entries and are to be ignored when creating the budget.
cases.oracle: The tester confirms the three fields are filled by the system from the entries, not by the user.

cases.section: How to Create Budgets and Manage Budgets
cases.title: Budget aggregate fields are calculated later (section-page description)
cases.why: The P2P section page independently states the allocated / spent / balance fields are aggregates; this confirms they are derived money fields.
cases.setup: Budget owner on the budget creation form.
cases.steps: 1. Open the budget creation form. 2. Leave allocated budget, spent budget and balance amount untouched. 3. Add categories in the Budget category list ('Plus new', select a category type, enter the budget allocated).
cases.expected: Allocated budget, spent budget and balance amount are aggregate fields calculated later, not filled on creation.
cases.oracle: The tester confirms the three fields reflect system aggregation after categories are added.

cases.title: Approver finds a pending budget request in Approvals and opens its Approval Note
cases.why: Approvers must be able to find and review the full budget before deciding.
cases.setup: Approver in the workflow of a submitted budget.
cases.steps: 1. Log in to Procol. 2. Go to the Approvals tab from the left-side navigation panel. 3. Locate the budget approval request pending your action and click it.
cases.expected: The Approval Note page appears with an Overview section (budget details) and a Details section (budget categories, amounts and workflow information).
cases.oracle: The Approval Note shows both sections with the submitted categories and amounts.

cases.title: Approver approves a budget (with optional remarks); workflow moves to the next approver
cases.why: Each approval must advance the budget along the configured sequence.
cases.setup: First approver in a multi-approver budget workflow.
cases.steps: 1. Open the budget's Approval Note from the Approvals tab. 2. Review the budget information. 3. (Optional) Add remarks in the remarks field. 4. Click Approve.
cases.expected: The approval is submitted and the workflow automatically moves to the next approver in the sequence.
cases.oracle: The workflow shows this approval recorded and the next approver as pending.

cases.title: Approver rejects a budget that needs changes
cases.why: Rejection stops a wrong budget becoming active.
cases.setup: Approver in the workflow of a submitted budget.
cases.steps: 1. Open the budget's Approval Note from the Approvals tab. 2. Add remarks describing the needed changes. 3. Click Reject.
cases.expected: The request is rejected; the budget does not reach Approved status.
cases.oracle: The tester confirms the request is no longer pending for this approver and the budget status is not Approved.

cases.title: Budget becomes Approved and active only after all approvers approve
cases.why: A budget that goes live after a partial approval would let spend start without full sign-off.
cases.setup: Submitted budget with two or more approvers.
cases.steps: 1. Have the first approver approve. 2. Check the budget status. 3. Have the remaining approver(s) approve. 4. Check the budget status again.
cases.expected: After the partial approval the budget is not yet Approved; when all approvers have approved, the budget status updates to Approved and the budget becomes active for the specified department and categories.
cases.oracle: Budget status reads Approved only after the last approval.

cases.title: Start a new contract with Contract ID, Name, Draft Status and Start Date
cases.why: Contracts are applied in intake and at PO level, so the contract record is part of the money flow; the article covers only the start of creation.
cases.setup: User with access to the Contracts page.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Contracts page from the left-side navigation panel. 2. Click "+ New". 3. On the Contract page, fill Contract ID, Contract Name, Draft Status and Start Date. 4. Click "Show More" and review the additional fields.
cases.expected: The Contract page accepts the required details; the article does not state what happens on save.
cases.oracle: The tester confirms the fields accept the values and records how the contract is saved (not described in the article).

cases.title: PR Approval (WF-PR-001): end-to-end order of steps
cases.why: Every pr approval must pass through the same governed chain; a skipped or reordered step is a control failure.
cases.setup: Trigger: Employee submits Purchase Requisition. Workflow WF-PR-001 as configured in the workbook (4 steps).
cases.steps: 1. Cause the trigger: employee submits Purchase Requisition. 2. Let step 1 "Budget Check" (System Validation, System (Auto)) complete. 3. Let step 2 "Line Manager Approval" (Approval, Requestor's Line Manager) complete with an approval. 4. Let step 3 "Finance Approval" (Approval, Finance Controller) complete with an approval. 5. Let step 4 "PR-to-PO Conversion" (System Action, System / Buyer) complete.
cases.expected: The steps run in this order: 1. Budget Check (System (Auto)) → 2. Line Manager Approval (Requestor's Line Manager) → 3. Finance Approval (Finance Controller) → 4. PR-to-PO Conversion (System / Buyer). At the end: Auto-converts to PO if template mapped; else Buyer manually creates PO.
cases.oracle: The workflow's history shows each step, its actor and its outcome in the order above, and nothing out of sequence.

cases.title: PR Approval: step 1 "Budget Check" runs automatically
cases.why: Step 1 is a System Validation step performed by System (Auto); if it does not run, everything after it rests on an unchecked premise.
cases.setup: Trigger: Employee submits Purchase Requisition.
cases.steps: 1. Cause the trigger: employee submits Purchase Requisition. 2. Let the workflow reach step 1 "Budget Check".
cases.expected: Step 1 is carried out by System (Auto) without manual action (workbook: "Checks available budget against GL code; blocks if exceeded"), and the workflow moves on.
cases.oracle: The workflow history records step 1 as done by System (Auto) and step 2 becomes active.

cases.title: PR Approval: step 1 "Budget Check" blocks if exceeded
cases.why: The workbook says the step "Checks available budget against GL code; blocks if exceeded". Letting the item through defeats the check.
cases.setup: Trigger: Employee submits Purchase Requisition. Workbook note for the step: Checks available budget against GL code; blocks if exceeded.
cases.steps: 1. Cause the trigger with an item for which the step's check fails — the "exceeded" case the note describes. 2. Let the workflow reach step 1.
cases.expected: The workflow is blocked at step 1 "Budget Check".
cases.oracle: No later step becomes active; the item is shown as blocked at step 1.

cases.title: PR Approval: step 2 "Line Manager Approval" routes to Requestor's Line Manager
cases.why: Approval 2 belongs to Requestor's Line Manager; routing it anywhere else puts the decision in the wrong hands.
cases.setup: Trigger: Employee submits Purchase Requisition. Approval mode: Sequential. Requestor's Line Manager user exists on the tenant.
cases.steps: 1. Cause the trigger: employee submits Purchase Requisition. 2. Complete the steps before step 2. 3. Check who has the pending approval.
cases.expected: The approval for step 2 "Line Manager Approval" is assigned to the Requestor's Line Manager, and only after the previous step has completed (sequential).
cases.oracle: The pending-approval record for step 2 names Requestor's Line Manager as the approver.

cases.title: PR Approval: step 2 "Line Manager Approval" is not routed before step 1 completes
cases.why: The approval mode is Sequential; an approver who sees an item before the previous level decides is approving out of order.
cases.setup: Trigger: Employee submits Purchase Requisition. Step 1 still pending.
cases.steps: 1. Cause the trigger. 2. Leave step 1 undecided. 3. Check the Requestor's Line Manager's pending approvals.
cases.expected: Nothing is pending for the Requestor's Line Manager at step 2 until step 1 completes.
cases.oracle: No step-2 approval record exists while step 1 is pending; it appears once that step completes.

cases.title: PR Approval: step 2 escalates to Department Head after 24h
cases.why: An approval left with the Requestor's Line Manager beyond its 24-hour SLA stalls the pr approval; escalation is the control that unblocks it.
cases.setup: Trigger: Employee submits Purchase Requisition. SLA for step 2: 24 hours; escalation to Department Head.
cases.steps: 1. Route an item to step 2 (Requestor's Line Manager). 2. Leave it undecided for more than 24 hours.
cases.expected: After 24 hours without action the approval escalates to the Department Head.
cases.oracle: The approval history shows the SLA breach and the Department Head as the new or added approver.

cases.title: PR Approval: step 2 does not escalate before 24h
cases.why: Escalating early takes the decision away from the Requestor's Line Manager before their SLA is up.
cases.setup: Trigger: Employee submits Purchase Requisition. SLA for step 2: 24 hours.
cases.steps: 1. Route an item to step 2 (Requestor's Line Manager). 2. Check its state shortly before 24 hours have passed.
cases.expected: The approval is still with the Requestor's Line Manager; nothing has gone to the Department Head.
cases.oracle: No escalation entry exists before the 24-hour mark.

cases.title: PR Approval: step 2 bypassed when "Amount ≤ INR 10,000 and vendor pre-approved"

cases.section: A Full Tour of the Purchase Requisitions Page
cases.title: ERP-raised PR appears automatically on Procol's PR page (integrated client)
cases.why: For integrated clients the PR page is fed by the ERP; if a PR raised in the ERP does not reflect in Procol, buyers never see the demand they must source.
cases.setup: Buyer on an integrated client (ERP such as SAP S4 Hana connected); access to the ERP to raise a PR.
cases.steps: 1. Raise a PR in the connected ERP. 2. Open the Purchase Requisitions page in Procol.
cases.expected: The PR's line items automatically reflect on Procol's PR page with their status.
cases.oracle: The ERP PR's line items are listed on the PR page without any manual entry in Procol.

cases.section: A Full Tour of the Purchase Requisitions Page
cases.title: PR line item moves from Open to In Progress once an event is created for it
cases.why: The status tabs are how buyers track progress; Open means no event exists and In Progress means one does, so the transition must follow event creation.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page; a PR line item in the Open tab (no events created for it).
cases.steps: 1. Confirm the line item is listed under the Open status tab. 2. Create an event for that line item. 3. Navigate between the status tabs.
cases.expected: Before the event the item is Open ("No Events have been created for this PR Line Item"); after the event it is In Progress ("Events have been created for this PR Line Item").
cases.oracle: The line item no longer appears under Open and appears under In Progress.

cases.section: A Full Tour of the Purchase Requisitions Page
cases.title: No events can be created for a PR line item on Hold
cases.why: Hold exists to stop sourcing on a line; if an event can still be created, held demand gets bought anyway.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page; a PR line item placed on Hold (via "🚫 Hold Item" with a remark).
cases.steps: 1. Open the Hold status tab and find the held line item. 2. Attempt to create an event for that line item.
cases.expected: No event can be created for the line item until it is taken out of Hold.
cases.oracle: The event cannot be created for the held line item; it stays in the Hold tab.

cases.section: How do I assign PRs to my Team?
cases.title: Assign a single PR line item to a team member
cases.why: Assignment makes a team member responsible for executing the purchase (creating events and moving the PR from Open to Completed).
cases.setup: Purchase manager on the PR page; at least one PR line item without an assignee.
cases.steps: 1. Hover over the "+" icon in the Assignee column of the line item. 2. Click "Add Assignee" when the option appears. 3. From the dropdown of available users, select the team member.
cases.expected: The line item is assigned to the selected team member.
cases.oracle: The Assignee column of that line item shows the selected team member.

cases.section: How do I assign PRs to my Team?
cases.title: Bulk-assign several PR line items at once
cases.why: Bulk assignment is how a whole PR, or items grouped by category or buyer responsibility, is handed to one person.
cases.setup: Purchase manager on the PR page; several unassigned PR line items.
cases.steps: 1. Select the line items by checking the boxes on the left. 2. Click the "Add Assignee" button at the top right. 3. Choose the user from the dropdown.
cases.expected: All selected line items are assigned to the chosen user.
cases.oracle: Each selected line item's Assignee column shows the chosen user; unselected items are unchanged.

cases.section: How do I hold a PR Line item?
cases.title: Hold a PR line item with a remark; it appears in the Hold tab with who held it
cases.why: Holding pauses a line item and removes it from processing; the Hold tab must record who held it.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page; a PR line item that is not on hold.
cases.steps: 1. Scroll to the far right of the PR table. 2. Click the "🚫 Hold Item" button for the line item. 3. Enter a remark explaining why the item is being held. 4. Confirm by clicking the blue "Hold Item" button. 5. Open the Hold status tab of the PR page.
cases.expected: The line item is placed on hold and is listed in the Hold status tab together with who it was held by.
cases.oracle: The item appears in the Hold tab showing the holder's name.

cases.section: How do I hold a PR Line item?
cases.title: Holding (and reopening) a PR line item signals the ERP to hold the item there too
cases.why: Procol and the ERP must agree on which items are held; otherwise the ERP keeps processing items paused in Procol.
cases.setup: Buyer on an integrated client with access to the ERP; a PR line item sourced from the ERP.
cases.steps: 1. Hold the line item in Procol ("Hold Item" with a remark, then confirm). 2. Check the same item in the ERP.
cases.expected: The hold action sends a signal to the ERP so the item is held there as well.
cases.oracle: The item shows as held in the ERP after the Procol hold.

cases.section: How do I reopen Line Items?
cases.title: Reopen a held PR line item; it returns to the Open tab
cases.why: Reopening brings a held line back into an Open state so it can be processed.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page; a line item on Hold.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Hold status tab of the PR page. 2. Scroll to the far right of the PR table. 3. Click the "♻️ Re-open Item" button for the line item. 4. Read the message and confirm by clicking the blue "Reopen Item" button. 5. Open the Open status tab.
cases.expected: The line item is reopened and is listed in the Open status tab.
cases.oracle: The item is gone from the Hold tab and present in the Open tab.

cases.section: How do I start processing my PRs
cases.title: Quantity can be edited directly in the cart
cases.why: Buyers often source part of a PR; the cart quantity is what flows into the project.
cases.setup: Buyer with PR line items in the cart side panel.
cases.steps: 1. Click on the quantity box of a cart line. 2. Type a new value lower than the requested quantity.
cases.expected: The quantity is editable and accepts the new value.
cases.oracle: The cart line shows the edited quantity.

cases.section: How do I start processing my PRs
cases.title: Edited cart quantity cannot exceed the PR's requested quantity
cases.why: Sourcing more than was requisitioned would buy unapproved quantity.
cases.setup: Buyer with a PR line item in the cart; the originally requested quantity is known.
cases.steps: 1. Click on the quantity box of the cart line. 2. Type a value greater than the originally requested quantity.
cases.expected: The edited quantity cannot exceed the originally requested quantity from the PR.
cases.oracle: The cart does not keep a quantity above the requested quantity.

cases.section: How do I start processing my PRs
cases.title: UOM of the quantity cannot be changed in the cart
cases.why: Changing the unit at this stage would silently change what is being bought.
cases.setup: Buyer with a PR line item in the cart.
cases.steps: 1. In the cart side panel, try to change the UOM of a line's quantity.
cases.expected: The UOM cannot be changed at this stage.
cases.oracle: The UOM stays the one from the PR.

cases.title: Selecting a Product Name auto-fills the Product Code
cases.why: The product code drives downstream PR/PO data; auto-fill prevents mismatched codes.
cases.setup: Requestor on the Product Details section of an intake request.
cases.steps: 1. Search and select a Product Name in a product row.
cases.expected: The Product Code is auto-filled from the selected product.
cases.oracle: The row's Product Code field is populated without being typed.

cases.section: How to Approve and Complete an Intake Request
cases.title: Remarks are optional when approving an intake
cases.why: The article calls remarks optional (but encouraged); approval must not be blocked when none are given.
cases.setup: Approver who is the current approver of a submitted intake request.
cases.steps: 1. Open the intake request. 2. Leave the Remarks / Comments field empty. 3. Click Approve.
cases.expected: The approval goes through without a remark.
cases.oracle: The workflow shows the approval with name and timestamp.

cases.section: How to Approve and Complete an Intake Request
cases.title: Approval workflow is selected by request category, line items or organisational policy
cases.why: Different requests must route to different approvers per policy; a wrong route bypasses the right approver.
cases.setup: A client with at least two approval policies that differ by request category (or line items / department).
cases.steps: 1. Submit one intake matching policy A (e.g. one category). 2. Submit another intake matching policy B (e.g. a different category). 3. Compare the approval workflows of the two intakes.
cases.expected: Each intake's workflow is selected according to the logic (request category, line items or organisational policy) it matches.
cases.oracle: The two flowcharts show the approvers configured for their respective policies.

cases.section: How to Raise a Purchase Intake Request

cases.why: Category drives the auto-assigned approval chain; the fields must appear when the condition needs them.
cases.setup: Requestor on the Create Intake Request page.
cases.steps: 1. Enter a Request Title. 2. Select the Request Condition "Material Creation".
cases.expected: Additional fields for Category and Subcategory appear, each with a dropdown of values.
cases.oracle: Category and Subcategory dropdowns are visible after the selection and not before.

cases.section: How to Raise a Material Creation Request via Intake
cases.title: Material Code is optional and can be left blank
cases.why: Requestors often do not know the code; leaving it blank must not block the request (it is generated later).
cases.setup: Requestor on the material creation fields of a Material Creation intake.
cases.steps: 1. Fill Item Description, Item Type, Unit of Measure (e.g. KG, NOS), Category and Subcategory. 2. Leave Material Code blank. 3. Click "Next" to the Approval Workflow.
cases.expected: The request proceeds with Material Code left blank, to be generated later.
cases.oracle: The Approval Workflow step is reached with no Material Code entered.

cases.section: How to Create Budgets and Manage Budgets

cases.why: A new budget must not be live before approval; Draft is the stated starting state.

cases.steps: 1. Click "+ New" on Budget Management. 2. Select the department name, the type and the fiscal year range. 3. Look at the status.
cases.expected: The status is automatically in the Draft state.
cases.oracle: The status field shows Draft without the user setting it.

cases.section: How to Create Budgets and Manage Budgets

cases.why: The article states a limit of up to 4 participant teams; the form must enforce it.

cases.steps: 1. Assign participant teams from the dropdown lists, one after another. 2. Try to assign a fifth team.
cases.expected: Up to 4 participant teams can be assigned; no fifth team can be added.
cases.oracle: Only four participant-team dropdowns / selections are available.

cases.section: How to Create Budgets and Manage Budgets

cases.section: How to Create Budgets and Manage Budgets
cases.title: Budget Creation page shows Budget Category List, Budget Update Request List and Purchase Requisition tabs

cases.expected: Three tabs: Budget Category List (category budgets), Budget Update Request List (view and manage update requests) and Purchase Requisition (PRs linked to the budget). The section page names the third tab "Purchase acquisition".
cases.oracle: The Purchase Requisition tab lists the PR linked to this budget.

cases.title: SAP PR Sync Mode (integration.sap.pr.sync_mode) = Push (SAP → Procol) (default)
cases.why: Different SAP landscapes have different integration capabilities. Some S/4HANA environments support event-driven push; others require scheduled polling. This config avoids hardcoding integration mode in code.
cases.setup: Persona: Tenant Admin. Plan: tenant on Enterprise (Plan Required: Enterprise). gate: `integration.sap.pr.sync_mode` = Push (SAP → Procol) (default: Push (SAP → Procol)) — CONF-INT-001 "SAP PR Sync Mode", Dropdown, risk if changed: High.
cases.steps: 1. As the Tenant Admin, set `integration.sap.pr.sync_mode` to Push (SAP → Procol). 2. As a Tenant Admin: use PR Sync Modes (Real-time / Batch) to get PR sync configurable as real-time or scheduled batch. 3. Observe the behaviour the setting controls: controls the direction of Purchase Requisition data flow between SAP and Procol.
cases.expected: With Push (SAP → Procol) selected, the behaviour follows it. What the setting controls: Controls the direction of Purchase Requisition data flow between SAP and Procol.
cases.oracle: The behaviour in step 3 matches Push (SAP → Procol).

cases.title: SAP PR Sync Mode (integration.sap.pr.sync_mode) = Pull (Procol polls SAP)

Stated business impact: Affects data freshness and system load; Bidirectional mode requires conflict resolution logic to be configured.
cases.oracle: The behaviour in step 3 matches Pull (Procol polls SAP) and differs from the default.

cases.section: A Full Tour of the Purchase Requisitions Page
cases.title: PR line item shows Completed when its requested quantity is fulfilled
cases.why: Completed must only mean the full PR quantity has been fulfilled; a premature Completed hides open demand.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page; a PR line item with events created (In Progress).
cases.steps: 1. Fulfil the full quantity for which the PR was raised for that line item. 2. Open the Completed status tab.
cases.expected: The line item falls under Completed ("The Quantity for which the PR has been raised for the Line Item has been fulfilled").
cases.oracle: The line item is listed in the Completed tab and not in In Progress.

cases.section: A Full Tour of the Purchase Requisitions Page
cases.title: Filters persist across pages and modules until "Clear Filter" is clicked
cases.why: Buyers filter items from different PRs to build a common event; losing filters on navigation breaks that workflow, and Clear Filter must fully restore the page.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page with line items from several PRs.
cases.steps: 1. Apply one or more filters on the PR page. 2. Switch to a different page or module of the platform, then return to the PR page. 3. Click the "🗑️ Clear Filter" button.
cases.expected: After returning, the filters are still applied; after Clear Filter, all filters are cleared and the page reverts to its original state.
cases.oracle: The filtered list is unchanged after navigation; after Clear Filter the unfiltered list is shown.

cases.section: A Full Tour of the Purchase Requisitions Page
cases.title: Exporting PRs sends the report to the user's email as an Excel document
cases.why: Export is the offline record of all PR line items; it is delivered by email rather than downloaded.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page with access to their mailbox.
cases.steps: 1. Click the export button on the PR page. 2. Check the user's email.
cases.expected: An export report of all PR line items and their details is sent to the user's email as an excel document (.csv / .xlsx).
cases.oracle: An email with the .csv/.xlsx export arrives containing the PR line items.

cases.section: How do I assign PRs to my Team?
cases.title: Assignee is responsible for creating events and moving the PR from Open to Completed
cases.why: The article defines what assignment means operationally; a tester should confirm the assignee can carry the line item through.
cases.setup: A PR line item assigned to a team member (buyer); the assignee logged in.
cases.steps: 1. As the assignee, open the PR page and find the assigned line item in Open. 2. Create sourcing events for it and progress it until its quantity is fulfilled.
cases.expected: The assignee can create events for the item and it moves from Open towards Completed.
cases.oracle: The line item's status tab changes from Open (to In Progress, then Completed) under the assignee's actions.

cases.section: How do I hold a PR Line item?
cases.title: A held item can be reopened at any time
cases.why: The article states hold is reversible at any time; a hold that cannot be undone would strand demand.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page; a line item on Hold.
cases.steps: 1. Open the Hold status tab. 2. Reopen the held item.
cases.expected: The item can be reopened whenever the user chooses.
cases.oracle: The item leaves the Hold tab after reopening.

cases.section: How do I reopen Line Items?
cases.title: A reopened line item is available for buying again
cases.why: The point of reopening is that the item can be sourced again; the hold restriction must lift.
cases.setup: Buyer on the PR page; a line item that was held and has just been reopened.
cases.steps: 1. Reopen the held line item ("Re-open Item", then "Reopen Item"). 2. Select it from the Open tab and start processing it (e.g. add it to the purchase cart / create an event).
cases.expected: The item is available for buying again and can be processed.
cases.oracle: The item can be selected and processed from the Open tab without the hold blocking it.

cases.section: How do I reopen Line Items?
cases.title: Requisitioner is notified when their line item is reopened
cases.why: The requisitioner owns the demand and must learn that a held item is back in play.
cases.setup: A held PR line item with a known requisitioner; access to the requisitioner's notifications.
cases.steps: 1. Reopen the held line item and confirm. 2. Check the requisitioner's notifications.
cases.expected: The requisitioner responsible for the item gets notified about the reopen action.
cases.oracle: A notification about the reopen reaches the requisitioner.

cases.section: How do I start processing my PRs
cases.title: Remove an item from the cart with the trash icon
cases.why: Buyers must be able to drop a line before it goes into a project.
cases.setup: Buyer with at least two PR line items in the cart.
cases.steps: 1. Click the "🗑️" trash icon next to one cart line.
cases.expected: That item is removed from the cart.
cases.oracle: The line no longer appears in the side panel and the item count drops by one.

cases.section: How do I start processing my PRs
cases.title: Cart supports proceeding to Technical Stage / RFQ / Reverse Auction or PO
cases.why: The article names the downstream procurement steps the cart prepares for; each should be reachable from a project.
cases.setup: Buyer with PR line items in the cart.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Create Project" in the cart. 2. Review the event types offered for the Sourcing Project.
cases.expected: The cart lets the buyer organise the items before steps like creating a Technical Stage / RFQ / Reverse Auction or PO.
cases.oracle: The tester confirms the event-type choices allow these downstream steps.

cases.title: Add multiple product rows and delete a row with the Red Bin icon
cases.why: One intake can request several materials; rows must be addable and removable before submission.
cases.setup: Requestor on the Product Details section with one filled product row.
cases.steps: 1. Click on the cell in the next row and fill Product Name, Quantity, Unit of Measure and Delivery Location. 2. Repeat for another row. 3. Click the Red Bin icon on one row.
cases.expected: A new blank row is added every time a next-row cell is used; the binned row is deleted.
cases.oracle: The product table shows the remaining rows only, plus a trailing blank row.

cases.title: Optional Vendor Information / Budget Information sections depend on form setup
cases.why: These sections are configuration-dependent; an intake must be submittable with them left empty when they are optional.
cases.setup: Requestor on a client whose intake form includes Vendor Information and/or Budget Information sections.
cases.steps: 1. Fill the mandatory intake details and product rows. 2. Leave (or fill) the Vendor Information / Budget Information sections. 3. Continue to the Approval Workflow and submit.
cases.expected: The sections appear according to the form setup and are optional.
cases.oracle: The intake proceeds to the Approval Workflow with the optional sections empty.

cases.title: Recover an unfinished intake draft with "Continue editing"
cases.why: Requestors who leave mid-way should not have to re-enter the request.
cases.setup: Requestor who started an intake request and left the page before submitting.
cases.steps: 1. Return to the Intake page. 2. Click "Continue editing" on the saved draft.
cases.expected: The saved draft is recovered with the previously entered details.
cases.oracle: The intake form reopens with the earlier values filled.

cases.section: How to Raise a Purchase Intake Request
cases.title: Add several products and delete a row before submitting the purchase intake
cases.why: Multi-line purchase requests are common; row add/delete must work before submission.
cases.setup: Requestor on the Product Details section of a purchase intake.
cases.steps: 1. Fill a first product row (Product Name, Quantity, Unit of Measure, Delivery Location). 2. Click on the cell in the next row and fill a second product. 3. Click the Red Bin icon on one row.
cases.expected: A new blank row is added every time; the binned row is deleted.
cases.oracle: Only the kept product rows remain in the table.

cases.section: How to Raise a Purchase Intake Request
cases.title: Material not in the catalogue: raise a Material Creation request instead
cases.why: The article directs requestors to the material creation flow when the material does not exist, rather than a free-text purchase.
cases.setup: Requestor raising a purchase intake for a material that does not exist in the system.
cases.steps: 1. In Product Details, search for the material by Product Name. 2. When it is not found, follow the article's pointer to raise a Material Creation request via Intake.
cases.expected: The material cannot be selected in the purchase intake, and the requestor is pointed to the Material Creation request flow.
cases.oracle: The tester confirms the material is absent from the Product Name search and the Material Creation intake is available.

cases.section: How to Raise a Purchase Intake Request
cases.title: Recover a purchase intake draft with "Continue editing"
cases.why: Saved drafts protect requestors from losing a partly filled request.
cases.setup: Requestor who started a purchase intake and left before submitting.
cases.steps: 1. Return to the Intake page. 2. Click "Continue editing".
cases.expected: The saved draft is recovered.
cases.oracle: The intake form reopens with the earlier entries.

cases.section: How to Raise a Material Creation Request via Intake
cases.title: Item Type offers "Material" or "Service"
cases.why: Item Type classifies the new master record; both values the article names must be selectable.
cases.setup: Requestor on the material creation fields of a Material Creation intake.
cases.steps: 1. Open the Item Type field. 2. Select "Material"; then change it to "Service".
cases.expected: Item Type lets the requestor choose between "Material" and "Service".
cases.oracle: Both options are offered and the chosen one is kept.

cases.section: How to Raise a Material Creation Request via Intake
cases.title: Request several materials in one intake and delete a row
cases.why: One Material Creation intake can carry multiple new materials; rows must be addable and removable.
cases.setup: Requestor with one material row filled.
cases.steps: 1. Click on the cell in the next row and fill a second material. 2. Click the Red Bin icon on one row.
cases.expected: A new blank row is added every time; the binned row is deleted.
cases.oracle: Only the kept material rows remain.

cases.section: How to Create Budgets and Manage Budgets
cases.title: Budget Management page shows Budget Department List and Budget Update Request List tabs
