cases.expected: The Best price is shown only after the vendor has revised their price at least n times.
cases.oracle: Best price is hidden before the nth revision and visible after it.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Traffic Light: green band is inclusive of the entered value
cases.why: An off-by-one in band edges puts vendors in the wrong colour.
cases.setup: Buyer creating a Traffic Light auction with green value X.
cases.steps: 1. Enter X for green. 2. Publish; have a vendor bid exactly at X (price or rank) and another just above X.
cases.expected: Green is assigned to all vendors whose price / rank is ≤ X; the value X itself is inclusive.
cases.oracle: The vendor at exactly X shows green; the vendor above X does not.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Traffic Light: yellow band covers above X up to and including Y
cases.why: The yellow band bounds must be applied exactly as configured.
cases.setup: Buyer creating a Traffic Light auction with green X and yellow Y.
cases.steps: 1. Enter X for green and Y for yellow. 2. Publish; have vendors bid at a value > X and ≤ Y, and at a value > Y.
cases.expected: Yellow is assigned to vendors whose price / rank is ≤ Y and > X.
cases.oracle: The vendor between X and Y (inclusive of Y) shows yellow; the vendor above Y does not.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Traffic Light: minimum revisions before colour is shown
cases.why: Colour visibility can be gated on vendor engagement.
cases.setup: Buyer creating a Traffic Light auction.
cases.steps: 1. Enable **"Set Minimum revision to show Traffic Light color"** and enter n. 2. Publish; as a vendor, revise the price fewer than n times, then n times.
cases.expected: The traffic light colour is shown only after the vendor has revised their price at least n times.
cases.oracle: Colour is hidden before the nth revision and visible after it.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Knockout configuration: offer basis, starting price, tick size, time difference
cases.why: These four settings define every Knockout round.
cases.setup: Buyer creating a Knockout auction.
cases.steps: 1. Select the offer basis: "Best Price" or "Total Amount". 2. Set the Starting Price. 3. Add the Tick Size (price difference between two successive offers). 4. Add the Time Difference (time between two successive offers).
cases.expected: All four settings are accepted and saved on the event.
cases.oracle: The configured values are shown on the event before publishing.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Dutch with "Offers on Best Price" requires a closing condition
cases.why: Without a closing condition a best-price Dutch auction has no defined end.
cases.setup: Buyer creating a Dutch auction.
cases.steps: 1. Select **"Offers on Best Price"**.
cases.expected: The buyer has to select the condition for closing the auction.
cases.oracle: A closing-condition selector is shown and must be filled.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Dutch with "Offers on Total Amount" hides the closing condition
cases.why: Total-amount Dutch auctions always close on a single vendor, so the condition must not be asked.
cases.setup: Buyer creating a Dutch auction.
cases.steps: 1. Select **"Offers on Total Amount"**.
cases.expected: No closing condition is needed; it is hidden because only single vendor closing is done.
cases.oracle: The closing-condition selector is not shown.

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Dutch configuration: starting and ending price, tick size, time difference
cases.why: These values define the Dutch price ladder and when it stops.
cases.setup: Buyer creating a Dutch auction.
cases.steps: 1. Set the Starting Price and Ending Price. 2. Add the Tick Size. 3. Add the Time Difference.
cases.expected: The settings are accepted and saved on the event.
cases.oracle: The configured values are shown on the event before publishing.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: QCS shows ranks per line item and next to vendor names
cases.why: Buyers decide awards from these ranks.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Responses tab; several vendors have bid.
cases.steps: 1. Scroll through the line items in the comparison.
cases.expected: The QCS assigns ranks to each vendor at line item level and next to the vendor's name.
cases.oracle: Each line item shows vendor ranks, and each vendor name shows a rank.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: L1 price is highlighted in green
cases.why: The lowest price must be unmistakable to the buyer.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Responses tab; several vendors have bid.
cases.steps: 1. Compare vendor prices on a line item.
cases.expected: The system automatically highlights the **L1 (Lowest)** price in green for each line item.
cases.oracle: The lowest price cell per line item is green.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Reject a bid and allow the seller to bid again
cases.why: Buyers must be able to discard an invalid bid without excluding the vendor.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Responses tab; a vendor has bid.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **three-dot menu** next to the vendor's name. 2. Select **Reject Bid**. 3. Check the box allowing the seller to bid again and confirm.
cases.expected: The bid is removed from the comparison view and the QCS, and the seller is allowed to bid again.
cases.oracle: The bid no longer appears in the QCS, and the vendor can still place a new bid.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Reject a bid without allowing the seller to bid again
cases.why: Buyers must be able to exclude a vendor from further bidding.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Responses tab; a vendor has bid.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **three-dot menu** next to the vendor's name and select **Reject Bid**. 2. Leave the allow-to-bid-again box unchecked and confirm.
cases.expected: The bid is removed from the comparison view and QCS, and the seller is not allowed to bid again.
cases.oracle: The bid is gone from the QCS, and the vendor cannot place a new bid.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Send a counter offer from the comparison view
cases.why: Counter offers are the buyer's negotiation lever during the auction.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Responses tab; a vendor has bid.
cases.steps: 1. Locate the vendor name in the comparison view. 2. Click the **Counter Offer** button under the vendor name.
cases.expected: The buyer is taken to the counter offer interface to configure and send revised expectations to the vendor.
cases.oracle: The counter offer interface opens for that vendor.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Show Best Prices reveals best price to suppliers and adds a QCS row
cases.why: Switching on best-price visibility changes what vendors see mid-auction.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Responses tab of a live rank-based auction.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **Actions** button. 2. Select **Show Best Prices**.
cases.expected: Suppliers see the exact best price for each line item, and the QCS gets an extra row per line item with the lowest bid across vendors.
cases.oracle: The vendor screen shows best prices; the buyer QCS shows the extra lowest-bid row.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Enable Vendor Masking hides vendor names and the participants tab
cases.why: Masking prevents bias while bidding is open.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Responses tab of a live auction.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **Actions** button. 2. Select **Enable Vendor Masking**.
cases.expected: All vendor names are hidden until bidding ends and replaced with Vendor 1, 2, 3 … N; the participants tab is also hidden.
cases.oracle: The QCS shows "Vendor 1", "Vendor 2"… instead of names, and the participants tab is not visible.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: View-Only Mode blocks counter offers, quote edits and surrogate bids
cases.why: View-only mode is a stated restriction used to freeze the auction for observers.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Responses tab of a live auction.
cases.steps: 1. Click **Actions** and select **Enable View-Only Mode**. 2. Try to send a counter offer, edit a quote and place a surrogate bid.
cases.expected: Users are restricted from sending counter offers, editing quotes or placing surrogate bids.
cases.oracle: None of the three actions can be performed while the mode is on.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Send a bulk counter offer to all vendors from Settings
cases.why: Bulk counter offers push all vendors at once during the auction.
cases.setup: Buyer on a live auction with several vendors bidding.
cases.steps: 1. Click on Settings and find "Send Bulk Counter Offers". 2. Decide the counter offer to send to all vendors and click on Send.
cases.expected: The counter offer is sent to all vendors.
cases.oracle: Each vendor has the counter offer on their side.

cases.title: During submission time, bids are on Sum Total and auto-broken down pro rata
cases.why: The pro-rata auto breakdown is what the buyer sees until vendors justify prices.
cases.setup: Live cost-breakdown auction; vendors have bid.
cases.steps: 1. As buyer, view the auction responses during submission time.
cases.expected: Vendors bid on the Sum Total only; all submissions appear as Auto-breakdown bids, broken down on a pro-rata basis.
cases.oracle: Each bid shows the vendor's total amount (highlighted) with pro-rata item values.

cases.title: Vendor reduces the Sum Total by a fixed value
cases.why: Fixed-value reduction is one of the two ways to bid in this mode.
cases.setup: Vendor in a live cost-breakdown auction with a Sum Total (e.g. ₹11,204.34).
cases.steps: 1. Keep "Fixed Value" in the dropdown and enter a reduction (e.g. ₹204.34). 2. Click **Revise Bid**.
cases.expected: The new current bid reflects the fixed reduction.
cases.oracle: The current bid equals the Sum Total minus the entered value.

cases.title: Vendor reduces the Sum Total by a percentage
cases.why: Percentage discount is the second way to bid in this mode.
cases.setup: Vendor in a live cost-breakdown auction.
cases.steps: 1. Select **"Percentage"** in the dropdown next to "Fixed Value" and enter a discount (e.g. 10%). 2. Click **Revise Bid**.
cases.expected: The new current bid reflects the percentage discount on the Sum Total.
cases.oracle: The current bid equals the Sum Total less the entered percentage.

cases.title: Cost Breakdown Time starts automatically when submission time ends
cases.why: The CBD window must open without buyer action or vendors cannot justify prices.
cases.setup: Live cost-breakdown auction nearing the end of submission time.
cases.steps: 1. Let the submission time end.
cases.expected: The Cost Breakdown Time (CBD time) begins automatically, and vendors are prompted to break down their total bid across line items.
cases.oracle: Buyer and vendor screens show the Cost Breakdown Time running.

cases.title: No line item may exceed its RFQ value in the breakdown
cases.why: Item prices above the RFQ quote would inflate the PO beyond what was offered.
cases.setup: Vendor during CBD time.
cases.steps: 1. Edit one line item price to a value greater than its RFQ value. 2. Try to submit.
cases.expected: The system does not allow an individual line item price greater than the RFQ value; an error message is shown.
cases.oracle: An error is displayed and the breakdown cannot be submitted.

cases.title: Breakdown total must match the auction bid, with amount to reduce shown
cases.why: The item prices must add up to the price the vendor won with.
cases.setup: Vendor during CBD time.
cases.steps: 1. Edit prices so the total exceeds the submitted auction bid. 2. Try to submit.
cases.expected: An error message is shown and the system indicates how much needs to be reduced further.
cases.oracle: The error states the remaining amount to reduce; submission is blocked until totals match.

cases.title: Submitted breakdown cannot be revised unless reopened or countered
cases.why: The article states a revision lock with two exceptions.
cases.setup: Vendor who has submitted a cost breakdown.
cases.steps: 1. As vendor, try to revise the submitted breakdown. 2. As buyer, reopen the window or share a counteroffer; retry as vendor.
cases.expected: The vendor cannot revise the breakdown unless the buyer reopens the window or shares counteroffers.
cases.oracle: Revision is blocked before the buyer action and possible after it (the article does not describe the reopen steps).

cases.title: Buyer sees the "Supplier Submitted CB" tag
cases.why: The buyer needs to know which vendors have justified their prices.
cases.setup: Buyer on a cost-breakdown auction; a vendor has submitted a breakdown.
cases.steps: 1. View that vendor's bid on the buyer screen.
cases.expected: The bid shows the **"Supplier Submitted CB"** tag.
cases.oracle: The tag is visible on the vendor's bid.

cases.section: How to create Serial Bidding events
cases.title: Total submission time is calculated from the number of line items
cases.why: The event end time must cover every line item's slot.
cases.setup: Buyer creating an auction with Serial Bidding enabled and a per-line-item duration.
cases.steps: 1. Add line items and watch the total submission time. 2. Add one more line item.
cases.expected: The system automatically calculates the total submission time based on the number of line items.
cases.oracle: The total submission time changes when the line item count changes.

cases.section: How to create Serial Bidding events
cases.title: Vendor can bid only on the current active line item
cases.why: This is the defining restriction of serial bidding.
cases.setup: Vendor in a live serial bidding auction with several line items.
cases.steps: 1. Place a bid on the current active line item. 2. Try to bid on another line item.
cases.expected: Vendors can only bid on the current active Line Item.
cases.oracle: Bidding works only on the active line item.

cases.section: How to create Serial Bidding events
cases.title: Upcoming line items are visible but not actionable
cases.why: Vendors can plan ahead without bidding out of turn.
cases.setup: Vendor in a live serial bidding auction.
cases.steps: 1. Look at an upcoming line item and try to act on it.
cases.expected: Vendors can view upcoming line items but cannot take any action on them.
cases.oracle: Upcoming items are listed with no enabled bid action.

cases.section: How to create Serial Bidding events
cases.title: Closed line items move to Ended Bidding with no further action
cases.why: Closed items must be frozen so late bids cannot land.
cases.setup: Vendor in a live serial bidding auction.
cases.steps: 1. Wait for the active line item's duration to end. 2. Look for it and try to act on it.
cases.expected: The line item moves to the **Ended Bidding** category, where no further action is possible.
cases.oracle: The item appears under Ended Bidding with no enabled actions.

cases.section: How to create Serial Bidding events
cases.title: Re-open closed line items with a new duration
cases.why: Buyers need a second chance on line items that closed too early.
cases.setup: Buyer on a serial bidding auction with at least one ended line item.
cases.steps: 1. On the buyer screen, go to **Settings**. 2. Click **Re-Open Line Items**; a side drawer opens. 3. Enter the new **duration** for each re-opened line item. 4. Select the line item(s) to re-open. 5. Click **Re-Open**.
cases.expected: The submission time restarts for the selected items.
cases.oracle: The selected items become active for bidding again with the new duration.

cases.section: How to Run a Price - Based Auction
cases.title: Buyer sees the best price among all bids
cases.why: Buyers track the current best price in price-based auctions.
cases.setup: Live Price Based auction; vendors have bid.
cases.steps: 1. As buyer, open the auction responses.
cases.expected: The buyer can see the best price among all bids.
cases.oracle: The best price shown equals the lowest submitted bid.

cases.section: How to Run a Price - Based Auction
cases.title: Vendors see the Best Price to beat
cases.why: Vendors must know which price to beat.
cases.setup: Live Price Based auction; vendors have bid.
cases.steps: 1. As vendor, open the auction.
cases.expected: The vendor can see the Best Price.
cases.oracle: The vendor screen shows the current best price.

cases.section: How to Run a Traffic Light Auction
cases.title: Traffic Light auction must award on the entire lot
cases.why: The article requires lot-level awarding for this strategy.
cases.setup: Buyer creating a Traffic Light auction.
cases.steps: 1. Select the Traffic Light strategy. 2. Check the awarding type, and try to use partial (line-item) awarding.
cases.expected: Awarding is on the entire lot for a Traffic Light auction.
cases.oracle: A tester confirms the event uses entire-lot awarding (the article does not state what happens with partial awarding).

cases.section: How to Run a Traffic Light Auction
cases.title: Traffic lights are assigned per the configured conditions
cases.why: Colour assignment is the output of the whole strategy.
cases.setup: Live Traffic Light auction; all vendors have submitted.
cases.steps: 1. As buyer, view the auction responses.
cases.expected: Traffic lights are assigned to vendors based on the conditions set by the buyer.
cases.oracle: Each vendor's colour matches the configured bands for their price/rank.

cases.section: How to Run a Traffic Light Auction
cases.title: Vendor sees their current zone and can bid to move zones
cases.why: Vendors improve bids by trial and error based only on their zone.
cases.setup: Vendor in a live Traffic Light auction.
cases.steps: 1. As vendor, view the current zone. 2. Revise the bid.
cases.expected: The vendor sees which zone they are in and can only use trial and error to move to a safer zone such as green or yellow.
cases.oracle: The zone shown updates after a revised bid crosses a band.

cases.section: How to Run a Knockout Auction
cases.title: Responses tab shows current round, upcoming offers and bidders
cases.why: Buyers monitor knockout rounds from this screen.
cases.setup: Published Knockout auction.
cases.steps: 1. Open the **Responses tab**.
cases.expected: It shows current round details (offer amount, tick size, time difference), upcoming offers and the list of bidders.
cases.oracle: All three sections are visible with the configured values.

cases.section: How to Run a Knockout Auction
cases.title: Each round presents a fixed offer stepped by the tick size
cases.why: The offer ladder must follow the configured tick size.
cases.setup: Published Knockout auction with starting price X and a tick size.
cases.steps: 1. Observe the offer in round 1 and in the following rounds.
cases.expected: Each round presents a fixed offer (₹X, then ₹X - Tick Size, and so on).
cases.oracle: Consecutive round offers differ by exactly the tick size.

cases.section: How to Run a Knockout Auction
cases.title: Vendor who accepts moves to the next round
cases.why: Acceptance is what keeps a vendor in the knockout.
cases.setup: Vendor in a live Knockout auction.
cases.steps: 1. Click **Accept** on the current offer.
cases.expected: The vendor moves forward to the next round.
cases.oracle: The vendor remains in the list of bidders for the next round.

cases.section: How to Run a Knockout Auction
cases.title: Vendor who does not accept is knocked out
cases.why: Only accepting vendors may continue; otherwise the last-man-standing rule fails.
cases.setup: Vendor in a live Knockout auction.
cases.steps: 1. Click **Not Accept** on the current offer.
cases.expected: The vendor does not move forward to the next round.
cases.oracle: The vendor is no longer among the bidders still in the running.

cases.section: How to Run a Dutch Auction.
cases.title: Responses tab shows round details including End Price
cases.why: Buyers monitor the Dutch ladder and its stop price from this screen.
cases.setup: Published Dutch auction.
cases.steps: 1. Open the **Responses tab**.
cases.expected: It shows current round details (offer amount, End Price, tick size, time difference), upcoming offers and the list of bidders.
cases.oracle: All sections are visible with the configured values.

cases.section: How to Run a Dutch Auction.
cases.title: End Price cannot be edited
cases.why: The End Price is the stated stop price; changing it mid-auction would alter the outcome.
cases.setup: Buyer on a published Dutch auction.
cases.steps: 1. Try to edit the End Price in the round controls.
cases.expected: The End Price cannot be edited.
cases.oracle: No edit control is available for the End Price, while tick size and time difference remain editable.

cases.section: How to Run a Dutch Auction.
cases.title: Next round offer moves by the tick size when no vendor accepts
cases.why: The price ladder must move exactly by the tick size toward the End Price.
cases.setup: Live Dutch auction with a starting price, tick size and End Price.
cases.steps: 1. Let a round pass with no vendor accepting. 2. Observe the next round's offer.
cases.expected: The next round starts with the offer being "Starting Price" + Tick Size, moving round by round until the End Price is reached.
cases.oracle: The new offer differs from the previous one by exactly the tick size.

cases.section: How to Run a Dutch Auction.
cases.title: Auction closes without award when End Price is reached with no acceptance
cases.why: The no-award outcome must be clean rather than awarding someone by default.
cases.setup: Live Dutch auction.
cases.steps: 1. Let every round pass without any vendor accepting until the End Price is reached.
cases.expected: The auction is closed without awarding to any vendor.
cases.oracle: The auction shows closed with no awarded vendor.

cases.section: How to setup a Technical Stage Event?
cases.title: Apply one RFP template to all line items via bulk Select Template
cases.why: The technical stage needs a template on every line item before vendors can respond.
cases.setup: Buyer creating a sourcing event that has a Technical Stage and several line items.
cases.steps: 1. Click on Technical Stage to review it. 2. Click on Select Template to apply an RFP Template for all the Line Items via Bulk Action.
cases.expected: The same template is applied to all line items.
cases.oracle: Every line item shows the selected RFP template.

cases.section: How to setup a Technical Stage Event?
cases.title: Assign a technical evaluator to a line item
cases.why: Without an evaluator nobody can rank the line item and the stage cannot complete.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Technical Stage of a sourcing event being created; the intended evaluator is a user in the org.
cases.steps: 1. Click on "+ Add Evaluator" under the first line item. 2. Search the user to assign as technical evaluator and select them.
cases.expected: The user is assigned as technical evaluator for that line item.
cases.oracle: The evaluator's name appears under the line item.

cases.section: How to setup a Technical Stage Event?
cases.title: Every line item needs an evaluator assigned
cases.why: The article says to repeat the assignment for all line items "without fail".
cases.setup: Buyer on the Technical Stage with several line items.
cases.steps: 1. Assign an evaluator to only some of the line items. 2. Try to proceed with the event.
cases.expected: Each line item must have a technical evaluator assigned.
cases.oracle: A tester checks whether the product flags or blocks line items without an evaluator (the article does not state the behaviour).

cases.section: How to run a Technical Stage Event?
cases.title: Send vendor submissions to evaluation
cases.why: Send to Evaluation hands the stage to the technical evaluators; without it nothing gets ranked.
cases.setup: Buyer with a published RFX event that has a Technical Stage; all vendors have submitted bids.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Technical Stage Tab. 2. Wait for the vendors to place their bids. 3. Click the blue **"Send to Evaluation"** button.
cases.expected: A notification is sent and the technical evaluator gets access to evaluate and assign technical ranks to all line items; the Evaluation time starts.
cases.oracle: The evaluator receives the notification and can open the stage for evaluation; an Evaluation time is shown.

cases.section: How to run a Technical Stage Event?
cases.title: Buyer cannot see technical evaluations before ranks are submitted and approved
cases.why: Technical results must stay hidden from the buyer until verified, to keep commercial decisions clean.
cases.setup: Buyer on a technical stage; the evaluator has not yet submitted ranks, or approval is pending.
cases.steps: 1. As buyer, open the Technical Stage while evaluation or approval is pending. 2. After the evaluator submits and all approvals are provided, open it again.
cases.expected: Only once the evaluator submits the technical rankings and the necessary approvals are provided can the buyer see the technical evaluations.
cases.oracle: Rankings are hidden before approval and visible after.

cases.section: How do I Evaluate a Technical Stage?
cases.title: Evaluator finds events marked "Evaluation Needed"
cases.why: Evaluators rely on the widget to know which events await them.
cases.setup: Technical Evaluator assigned to an event that has been sent to evaluation.
cases.steps: 1. Log in and navigate to the **Events** page. 2. Locate the event. 3. Click on it to open the **Project Details** page.
cases.expected: The event card carries a status widget "Evaluation Needed", and clicking it opens Project Details.
cases.oracle: The "Evaluation Needed" widget is on the card and the Project Details page opens.

cases.section: How do I Evaluate a Technical Stage?
cases.title: Evaluate line items and submit the score for approval
cases.why: Submitting scores creates the Technical Recommendation that goes to approval.
cases.setup: Technical Evaluator on an event with vendor submissions and an approval workflow configured.
cases.steps: 1. From **Project Details**, click the **Technical Stage** tab. 2. In a submission's evaluation section click the plus icon / **"Add Evaluation"**. 3. Select a rank and add a remark, then click **"OK"**; repeat for all vendors and line items. 4. Click **"Submit Score"** (blue, top right). 5. Select an Approval Workflow and click Next. 6. Enter closing remarks, review the workflow and click **"Submit"**.
cases.expected: The evaluation is sent for approval and the evaluator is taken to the **Approval Page** showing workflow progress.
cases.oracle: The Approval Page is displayed with the workflow progress.

cases.section: How do I Evaluate a Technical Stage?
cases.title: Remarks are mandatory to submit an evaluation
cases.why: The article states remarks are required; evaluations without justification must not be accepted.
cases.setup: Technical Evaluator adding an evaluation.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Add Evaluation", select a rank and leave the remark empty. 2. Click "OK".
cases.expected: The evaluation cannot be submitted without a remark.
cases.oracle: The evaluation is not saved until a remark is entered.

cases.section: How do I Evaluate a Technical Stage?
cases.title: Approval workflow is chosen by conditions when submitting scores
cases.why: The routing decides who must approve the technical recommendation.
cases.setup: Technical Evaluator who has completed all evaluations; workflows with conditions exist.
cases.steps: 1. Click **"Submit Score"**. 2. Select an approval workflow and click Next.
cases.expected: The evaluator selects an Approval Workflow based on conditions such as the number of DNA vendors or line items.
cases.oracle: The closing-remarks dialog shows the selected approval workflow for review.

cases.section: How do I Request for Revaluation?
cases.title: Buyer requests re-evaluation of selected line items
cases.why: Re-evaluation is the buyer's route to correct a disputed technical ranking.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Owner on a sourcing event in Evaluation Time with line items in "TR Submitted".
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the Technical Stage of the sourcing event. 2. Click the "Settings" dropdown and select "Request for Re-Evaluation." 3. In the "Request Re-Evaluation" side drawer, fill in the reason. 4. Under "Select Line Items," choose the line items. 5. Click the blue "Send Request" button.
cases.expected: The selected line items are marked as "Re-evaluation Requested," and the technical evaluators must take action.
cases.oracle: The line items show the status "Re-evaluation Requested."

cases.section: How do I Request for Revaluation?
cases.title: Request for Re-Evaluation is enabled only in Evaluation Time
cases.why: The article restricts re-evaluation requests to the evaluation window.
cases.setup: Buyer on a sourcing event outside Evaluation Time, and one inside it.
cases.steps: 1. Open the "Settings" dropdown on the Technical Stage outside Evaluation Time. 2. Repeat inside Evaluation Time.
cases.expected: "Request for Re-Evaluation" is enabled only in the Evaluation Time.
cases.oracle: The option is disabled outside Evaluation Time and enabled inside it.

cases.section: How do I Request for Revaluation?
cases.title: Re-evaluation reason is mandatory
cases.why: Evaluators need to know why re-evaluation is requested.
cases.setup: Buyer with the "Request Re-Evaluation" drawer open.
cases.steps: 1. Select line items but leave the reason empty. 2. Try to click "Send Request".
cases.expected: The request cannot be sent without a reason.
cases.oracle: The request is not sent and the line items do not change status.

cases.section: How do I Request for Revaluation?
cases.title: Only "TR Submitted" line items are eligible for re-evaluation
cases.why: Items not yet evaluated must not be sent back.
cases.setup: Buyer with the "Request Re-Evaluation" drawer open; the event has line items in "TR Submitted" and others not.
cases.steps: 1. Look at "Select Line Items" and try to select a line item not in "TR Submitted".
cases.expected: Only items in the "TR Submitted" stage are eligible.
cases.oracle: Non-"TR Submitted" items cannot be selected.

cases.section: How do Re-Evaluate Line items in Technical Stage?
cases.title: Evaluator accepts a re-evaluation request and resubmits
cases.why: Accepting is how disputed ranks get corrected.
cases.setup: Technical Evaluator on an event with line items marked "Re-evaluation Requested".
cases.steps: 1. Open the Technical Stage and identify the "Re-evaluation Requested" line items. 2. Review the reason and choose **Accept**; click "Accept and Re-evaluate" in the confirmation dialog. 3. Modify the technical scores and recommendations (e.g. reassign T1, T2). 4. Click Submit under the TR status widget. 5. Add closing remarks, select the approval flow if workflows are enabled, and click **Submit**.
cases.expected: The updated evaluation is finalised.
cases.oracle: The confirmation "You have successfully Re-evaluated the Line Items!" is shown with the updated ranks.

cases.section: How do Re-Evaluate Line items in Technical Stage?
cases.title: Evaluator rejects a re-evaluation request; ranks stay unchanged
cases.why: The evaluator can stand by the original evaluation.
cases.setup: Technical Evaluator on an event with line items marked "Re-evaluation Requested".
cases.steps: 1. Open the Technical Stage and choose **Reject** on the request. 2. In the dialog listing the line items, enter a rejection reason. 3. Click **Reject Re-evaluation**.
cases.expected: The technical rankings remain unchanged and the status returns to "TR Submitted."
cases.oracle: The line items show "TR Submitted" with their original ranks.

cases.section: How do Re-Evaluate Line items in Technical Stage?
cases.title: Rejection reason is mandatory before Reject Re-evaluation is enabled
cases.why: The buyer must learn why their request was rejected.
cases.setup: Technical Evaluator with the reject dialog open.
cases.steps: 1. Leave the rejection reason empty and look at the **Reject Re-evaluation** button. 2. Enter a reason.
cases.expected: The reason is mandatory; the button becomes clickable (turns blue) only after a reason is entered.
cases.oracle: The button is inactive with an empty reason and turns blue once text is entered.

cases.section: Surrogate Bidding: How to Place Bids on Behalf of Vendors
cases.title: Surrogate bids are visibly distinguished from vendor-placed bids in the QCS
cases.why: Evaluators and approvers must be able to tell which bids a buyer keyed in; the article defines the marker.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. An RFQ event where one vendor bid on the platform and another vendor's bid was entered as a surrogate bid.
cases.steps: 1. Open the RFQ stage QCS. 2. Compare the header of the surrogate-bid vendor with the vendor who bid themselves.
cases.expected: Only the surrogate-bid vendor carries the surrogate marker.
cases.oracle: "Surrogate Bid" appears in blue text under the surrogate vendor's name next to the currency, and is absent for the self-bidding vendor.

cases.section: How to Send and Manage Counter Offers?
cases.title: Quantity counter offer for partial awarding per line item
cases.why: The article's note says adjusting the quantities field in a counter offer enables partial awarding per line item — this changes how much is bought from each vendor.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. RFQ event with a vendor bid on a line item in the QCS.
cases.steps: 1. Open the QCS on the RFQ tab and click **"Counter Offer"** beneath the vendor's name. 2. Select the Quantity field. 3. Enter an adjusted (reduced) quantity. 4. Click **"Send Counter Offer"**.
cases.expected: The counter offer with the adjusted quantity is sent, enabling partial awarding for that line item.
cases.oracle: Success tooltip appears; the "Counter Offer Requested" tag shows above the vendor's name and the quantity cell is highlighted with original vs counter offer quantity.

cases.section: How to Send and Manage Counter Offers?
cases.title: Buyer revokes a pending counter offer
cases.why: A buyer must be able to withdraw a counter offer sent in error before the vendor acts on it.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. A vendor in the QCS with the "Counter Offer Requested" tag.
cases.steps: 1. Open the QCS on the RFQ tab. 2. Click **"Revoke Counter Offer"** under the vendor's name.
cases.expected: The counter offer is revoked.
cases.oracle: A tooltip confirms the counter offer has been revoked; the "Counter Offer Requested" tag is no longer shown for that vendor.

cases.section: How do I Modify Counter Offers as a Vendor?
cases.title: Counter Offer Banner shown to the vendor on receipt of a counter offer
cases.why: The banner is how the vendor learns a counter offer is waiting; without it the negotiation stalls.
cases.setup: Vendor persona. Buyer has sent a counter offer on an RFQ event.
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, open the RFQ event. 2. Look above the line item or vendor quote sheet.
cases.expected: The Counter Offer Banner is displayed.
cases.oracle: A Counter Offer Banner appears above the line item or vendor quote sheet.

cases.section: How do I Modify Counter Offers as a Vendor?
cases.title: Decline option offers both decline and modify
cases.why: The article states the system prompts the vendor to either decline or modify, so a vendor who disagrees is not forced into outright rejection.
cases.setup: Vendor persona. RFQ event with a pending counter offer.
cases.steps: 1. Open the RFQ event and the Counter Offer Banner. 2. Click on the counter offer Decline option.
cases.expected: A dialogue box for declining the counter offer opens and offers the choice to decline or to modify.
cases.oracle: The dialogue shows a decline choice and a **"Modify Counter Offer"** choice.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: Master QCS tab shows the evaluation summary on the latest commercial stage
cases.why: The MQCS is the basis for the award decision; missing prices, rankings or charges lead to wrong awards.
cases.setup: Buyer persona involved in awarding after commercial negotiation. An event whose RFQ or auction stage has vendor bids.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the latest commercial stage (RFQ or auction). 2. Click on the **Master QCS** tab.
cases.expected: The MQCS shows final and initial price comparisons, technical and commercial rankings, custom columns per client configuration and charges across stages.
cases.oracle: Master QCS tab displays final vs initial prices, technical and commercial ranks, configured custom columns and charges per stage.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: Award dialog allows modifying the quantity to award
cases.why: The dialog lets the buyer award less than the full quantity (split award); the proposal value must follow the awarded quantity.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. Awarding screen open for a line item with bids from at least two vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Select the checkbox for a vendor under the line item. 2. In the dialog, modify the quantity to award to a part of the line quantity. 3. Click **"Award"**.
cases.expected: Only the modified quantity is awarded to the vendor.
cases.oracle: The awarded quantity shown for the vendor equals the value entered, and the Proposal value reflects that quantity.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: Only approvers can take Approve or Reject action
cases.why: The article states the Approve / Reject action is for approvers; a non-approver able to approve would bypass the compliance chain.
cases.setup: Two users: one in the proposal's approval chain, one buyer not in it. A submitted award proposal.
cases.steps: 1. As the non-approver buyer, open the proposal's Approval Screen. 2. As the approver, open the same Approval Screen.
cases.expected: Approve / Reject actions are available to the approver and not to the non-approver.
cases.oracle: The non-approver's screen shows no Approve / Reject action; the approver's screen shows both.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: Approver finds the proposal via the Approvals tab and adds remarks
cases.why: Approvers reach proposals from the left navigation, not from the event; the NFA must be reviewable with remarks before deciding.
cases.setup: A user who is an approver on a submitted award proposal.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the **"Approvals"** tab in the left navigation panel. 2. Click on the event to view for approval. 3. On the Approvals/Proposals page, review the NFA and Proposal and leave remarks. 4. Approve or reject accordingly.
cases.expected: The event is listed on the approvals page and the approver can review, remark and act.
cases.oracle: The event appears on the approvals page; the Approvals/Proposals page shows the NFA and Proposal; the remark is saved with the decision.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: No purchase order request while approvals are still pending
cases.why: The article conditions PO generation on all approvals being received; an early PO would bypass approvers still in the chain.
cases.setup: An award proposal with an approval chain of at least two approvers.
cases.steps: 1. Have only the first approver approve the proposal. 2. Open the **"Purchase Orders"** tab.
cases.expected: No purchase order is requested for the event until the remaining approvals are received.
cases.oracle: The "Purchase Orders" tab shows no purchase order for the event; the approval chain shows the remaining approvers as pending.

cases.section: How to approve an Awarding proposal?
cases.title: Awarding proposal appears in the Approvals list once submitted
cases.why: The article states an approval is triggered after awarding and proposal creation; if it never reaches the approver, the award is stuck.
cases.setup: Buyer has completed awarding and proposal creation for a sourcing project; approver user in the chain.
cases.steps: 1. As the approver, navigate to the **"Approvals"** tab in the left navigation panel.
cases.expected: The sourcing event is listed on the approvals page.
cases.oracle: The event appears on the approvals page for the approver.

cases.section: How to approve an Awarding proposal?
cases.title: Approvals/Proposals page shows the sourcing event details for review
cases.why: The approver decides on what this page shows; the article names allocations summary and overview.
cases.setup: Approver user; an awarding proposal pending their approval.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the **"Approvals"** tab. 2. Click on the event.
cases.expected: The Approvals/Proposals page shows the details of the sourcing event including the allocations summary and overview, with the NFA and Proposal.
cases.oracle: Page displays the allocations summary, overview, NFA and Proposal for the event.

cases.section: How to approve an Awarding proposal?
cases.title: PO request waits for every approval in the chain
cases.why: "Once all the approvals have been received" is a stated condition — a partial approval must not trigger the ERP request.
cases.setup: An awarding proposal with at least two approvers.
cases.steps: 1. First approver approves via the **"Approvals"** tab. 2. Open the **"Purchase Orders"** tab. 3. Second approver approves. 4. Open the **"Purchase Orders"** tab again.
cases.expected: No purchase order is requested after only the first approval; it is requested after the final approval.
cases.oracle: "Purchase Orders" tab shows no PO for the event after step 2 and lists it after step 4.

cases.title: Auto sizing is only available in horizontal view
cases.why: The article states the Auto button is **ONLY AVAILABLE IN HORIZONTAL VIEW**; showing it elsewhere would be a defect.
cases.setup: Buyer, Technical Evaluator or Category Manager; an event with vendor quotes in the QCS.
cases.steps: 1. Open the QCS and switch to vertical view with the layout toggle. 2. Look for the **Auto** button. 3. Switch to horizontal view. 4. Look for the **Auto** button.
cases.expected: The Auto sizing option is not available in vertical view and is available in horizontal view.
cases.oracle: Auto button absent (or unavailable) in vertical view; present with Small/Medium/Large/XL in horizontal view.

cases.title: Participants tab is hidden from buyers when masking is enabled
cases.why: The article states the Participants tab is hidden so buyers cannot see who has or hasn't participated; leaving it visible defeats masking.
cases.setup: Buyer on a live RFQ or Auction event with Vendor Masking enabled.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event screen after enabling Vendor Masking. 2. Look for the Participants tab.
cases.expected: The Participants tab is hidden from the buyer.
cases.oracle: No Participants tab is shown on the event screen for the buyer.

cases.title: Vendor names stay masked until bidding ends
cases.why: The article scopes masking to "until bidding ends"; names leaking mid-bidding, or never returning afterwards, are both defects.
cases.setup: Buyer on a live RFQ or Auction event with Vendor Masking enabled.
cases.steps: 1. While bidding is live, view vendor names on the event screen. 2. Let bidding end. 3. View vendor names again.
cases.expected: Names remain as Vendor 1 … N throughout bidding; the masking applies only until bidding ends.
cases.oracle: During bidding only Vendor 1 … N labels are visible; after bidding ends the tester checks whether real vendor names are shown.

cases.section: How to enable Show Best Price?
cases.title: Buyer enables Show Best Prices and the QCS gains a best-price row
cases.why: Show Best Price exposes the current L1 price per line item, changing vendor bidding behaviour; the displayed value must be the true lowest bid.
cases.setup: Buyer, Auction Owner or Sourcing Manager on an event with bids from several vendors on line items.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **Actions** button. 2. Select **Show Best Prices**. 3. Open the QCS.
cases.expected: An extra row is added for each line item displaying the lowest bid across vendors.
cases.oracle: Each line item in the QCS has an additional row whose value equals the lowest vendor bid for that line item.

cases.section: How to enable Show Best Price?
cases.title: Participating vendors see the exact best price per line item
cases.why: The article states the best price is visible to both buyers and participating vendors so vendors know the price to beat to become L1.
cases.setup: Buyer has enabled **Show Best Prices** on an event; a participating vendor login.
cases.steps: 1. As a participating vendor, open the event. 2. View the line items.
cases.expected: The vendor sees the exact best price (lowest / L1 bid) for each line item.
cases.oracle: The vendor's view shows the best price per line item, matching the buyer's best-price row.

cases.title: Technical Evaluation Modes: refused for a user without the Buyer role
cases.why: The workbook names Buyer as the user of Technical Evaluation Modes. If any role can do it, the intended separation of duties is gone.
cases.setup: Persona: a user who holds none of these roles: Buyer. Plan: any tenant (Plan Required: All Plans). Status: GA.
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as that user on the tenant described in Setup. 2. Try it: use Technical Evaluation Modes to get evaluators to evaluate per line item or per vendor against a template. 3. Repeat as a Buyer.
cases.expected: The user without the role cannot carry out the action — Procol refuses it or does not offer it — while the Buyer can. (If the tenant's RBAC deliberately grants it to more roles, record that configuration rather than a defect.)
cases.oracle: Same tenant, same steps, different role: refused or absent for the other user, available to the Buyer.

cases.title: Department/Location-Based Evaluator Mapping: happy path for the Tenant Admin
cases.why: Accurate routing at scale. Business use: Technical evaluation auto-routes to evaluators mapped by department or site.
cases.setup: Persona: Tenant Admin. Plan: tenant on Enterprise (lowest plan with access; Plan Required: Enterprise). Status: GA.
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as a Tenant Admin on the tenant described in Setup and open RFP / Technical. 2. Use Department/Location-Based Evaluator Mapping to get what the story asks for: evaluation auto-routed by department or location. 3. Follow the business scenario the workbook gives: "Technical evaluation auto-routes to evaluators mapped by department or site". 4. Check the result against the story's promised outcome.
cases.expected: The Tenant Admin achieves the story's outcome: the right experts evaluate at scale. The business use case is served: technical evaluation auto-routes to evaluators mapped by department or site.
cases.oracle: Observable proof that Department/Location-Based Evaluator Mapping did its job for the Tenant Admin — the outcome in Expected is visible in Procol after the last step, with no error, on the plan in Setup. Any gap is a defect against FEAT-RFP-012.

cases.title: Department/Location-Based Evaluator Mapping: not available on the Growth plan
cases.why: The workbook limits Department/Location-Based Evaluator Mapping to "Enterprise". A tenant on a lower plan must not get it, or plan packaging is not enforced.
cases.setup: Persona: Tenant Admin. Plan: tenant on the Growth plan (Plan Required: Enterprise). Status: GA.
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as a Tenant Admin on the lower-plan tenant. 2. Try it: use Department/Location-Based Evaluator Mapping to get evaluation auto-routed by department or location. 3. Repeat on a tenant on Enterprise.
cases.expected: On the Growth plan the capability is not available to use. On Enterprise the same steps work.
cases.oracle: Same user role, same steps, different plan: refused or absent on the lower plan, available on Enterprise.

cases.title: Lot-Basis Re-evaluation: happy path for the Buyer
cases.why: Flexible re-evaluation scope. Business use: Re-evaluation is run at lot level when a lot-wide technical result is challenged.

Follow the business scenario the workbook gives: "Re-evaluation is run at lot level when a lot-wide technical result is challenged". 4. Check the result against the story's promised outcome.
cases.expected: The Buyer achieves the story's outcome: challenge a lot-level technical result. The business use case is served: re-evaluation is run at lot level when a lot-wide technical result is challenged.
cases.oracle: Observable proof that Lot-Basis Re-evaluation did its job for the Buyer — the outcome in Expected is visible in Procol after the last step, with no error, on the plan in Setup. Any gap is a defect against FEAT-RFP-014.

cases.title: Allow Partial Bidding (rfq.bid.allow_partial) = ON
cases.why: For large RFQs with many line items, forcing full bids limits vendor participation. Partial bidding increases competition and can reduce overall cost by splitting award across specialists.
cases.setup: Persona: Tenant Admin and Buyer. Plan: tenant on Growth (Plan Required: Growth, Enterprise). gate: `rfq.bid.allow_partial` = ON (default: OFF) — CONF-RFQ-001 "Allow Partial Bidding", Toggle, risk if changed: Medium.
cases.steps: 1. As the Tenant Admin, set `rfq.bid.allow_partial` to ON. 2. As a Buyer: use RFQ Templates (Line/Global/Formula) to get configurable RFQ templates with line and global terms and formulas. 3. Observe the behaviour the setting controls: when ON, vendors can submit bids for a subset of line items in the RFQ rather than the full BOQ.
cases.expected: With the setting ON, the behaviour follows it. What the setting controls: When ON, vendors can submit bids for a subset of line items in the RFQ rather than the full BOQ. Stated business impact: Enabling this requires Procurement team to handle split-award decisions and manage multiple POs; disabling ensures single-source RFQ completion.
cases.oracle: The behaviour in step 3 matches the ON setting; compare with the case for the other value — they must differ as the description states.
