cases.section: How to create a Single Stage Event (RFP, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: New Single Stage event defaults to Rank on Line and offers three event types
cases.why: A wrong default event type silently turns an intended RFQ into a reverse auction.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on the Events page.
cases.steps: 1. Click "+ New Event" and choose "Single Stage". 2. Observe the Event Type on the event setup screen. 3. Click the **Rank on Line** badge.
cases.expected: By default the Event Type is **Rank on Line** (a type of Reverse Auction); clicking the badge opens a side drawer with exactly three options: RFP (Request for Proposal), RFQ (Request for Quotation), Reverse Auction.
cases.oracle: Badge text on the setup screen reads Rank on Line; the side drawer lists the three event types.

cases.section: How to create a Single Stage Event (RFP, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Adding a product auto-adds a new row; typing narrows the product search
cases.why: Line-item entry is the bulk of event creation effort; the auto-row and search behaviours are what the article promises.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on the Single Stage event setup screen with a template selected.
cases.steps: 1. Click the cell beneath the "Products" column and type part of a product name. 2. Select the product from the dropdown.
cases.expected: Typing narrows the product dropdown; after a product is added a new empty row is automatically added beneath it.
cases.oracle: Dropdown options filter to the typed text; row count increases by one after selection.

cases.section: How to create a Single Stage Event (RFP, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Add vendors manually from Participants
cases.why: Buyers must be able to invite vendors that are not suggested by product mapping.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on the event setup screen.
cases.steps: 1. Click on Participants. 2. Search or filter for a vendor on the screen that shows up. 3. Add the vendor.
cases.expected: The Participants screen opens with search and filter; the chosen vendor is added as a participant.
cases.oracle: The manually added vendor is listed among the event's participants.

cases.section: How to create a Single Stage Event (RFP, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Event title is auto-generated from product and location and is editable
cases.why: Vendors see the title in invitations; it must be meaningful and correctable.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on the event setup screen with a product and location filled.
cases.steps: 1. Observe the event title after adding a product and location. 2. Edit the title text.
cases.expected: Procol auto-generates the event title using product and location names; the buyer can edit it.
cases.oracle: The initial title contains the product and location names; the edited title persists on the event.

cases.section: How to create a Single Stage Event (RFP, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: "Edit Schedule" from the publish pop-up schedules the event for later
cases.why: Buyers must be able to defer going live instead of publishing immediately.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager with a fully filled Single Stage event.
cases.steps: 1. Click the blue "Publish Event" button. 2. In the pop-up, press "Edit Schedule" instead of "Publish". 3. Set a later start.
cases.expected: The event is scheduled for later rather than going Live immediately.
cases.oracle: The event's schedule shows the future start; vendors are not invited as live until then (tester verifies at the article's level of detail).

cases.section: How to create a Sourcing Project (Technical Stage, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Project cart: edit quantity, change UOM, remove items, item count on Create Project
cases.why: Quantities and units chosen in the cart flow into every stage of the project.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager in the "eRFX Project" side drawer with at least two line items added.
cases.steps: 1. Click a quantity box in the cart and type a new value. 2. Click the small dropdown near the UOM, search, and select a different UOM. 3. Click the trash icon next to one line. 4. Look at the "Create Project" button.
cases.expected: Quantity is editable in the cart; the UOM changes to the selected one; the trashed item is removed; the "Create Project" button shows how many items are selected.
cases.oracle: Cart rows reflect the new quantity and UOM, the removed row is gone, and the count on "Create Project" matches the remaining rows.

cases.section: How to create a Sourcing Project (Technical Stage, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Selecting a template prefills products and quantities; Technical Stage bulk template applies to all line items
cases.why: Templates drive what vendors are asked for; bulk apply must reach every line item.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on the project creation screen with a Technical Stage and RFQ.
cases.steps: 1. On the RFQ tab click Select Template and choose a predefined template. 2. Click on Technical Stage, then Select Template to apply an RFP template via Bulk Action.
cases.expected: Products and quantities are prefilled after selecting the template; on the Technical Stage, the same template is applied for all line items.
cases.oracle: RFQ table shows the cart's products and quantities; every Technical Stage line item shows the chosen RFP template.

cases.section: How to create a Sourcing Project (Technical Stage, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Vendor-wise technical evaluation moves the evaluator to the Vendor Assessment section
cases.why: Alternate evaluation mode lets one person evaluate all line items.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on the Technical Stage of a project.
cases.steps: 1. Click on Technical stage under Event Type. 2. Switch to Vendor wise evaluation. 3. Add the Evaluator in the Vendor Assessment section.
cases.expected: All line items are evaluated by one person; the evaluator is added in the Vendor Assessment section rather than per line item.
cases.oracle: Evaluator field appears in the Vendor Assessment section instead of under each line item.

cases.section: How to create a Sourcing Project (Technical Stage, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Project-level actions: attachments, project-level T&Cs, Manage Items
cases.why: Project-level artefacts apply across stages and are distinct from stage-level ones.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager on the project creation screen.
cases.steps: 1. Add Project Level Attachments. 2. Add Project Level T&Cs. 3. Click Manage Items.
cases.expected: Attachments and T&Cs are added at project level (project T&Cs are different from event-specific T&Cs but follow the same method); Manage Items opens the cart functionality.
cases.oracle: Project shows the attachment and T&Cs; the cart opens on Manage Items.

cases.section: How to set Savings references in an Event?
cases.title: Line Item savings based on Price vs Total Amount
cases.why: Price is quantity-independent while Total Amount multiplies by quantity; choosing wrongly misstates savings.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement manager creating a new event with line items of quantity greater than 1.
cases.steps: 1. Open the "Savings" panel and select **Line Item**. 2. Choose **Price** and enter reference values per line item. 3. Switch to **Total Amount**.
cases.expected: With Price, savings are per unit excluding quantity; with Total Amount, savings are calculated on price multiplied by quantity.
cases.oracle: Tester compares computed savings on the evaluation/award view against reference × 1 vs reference × quantity (the article does not show the savings output screen).

cases.section: How to set Savings references in an Event?
cases.title: Add a custom savings reference
cases.why: Custom strategies (e.g. Best Price) extend the three defaults.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement manager with the Savings panel open.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Add a Custom Reference". 2. Type a name (e.g. Best Price) and click "Save". 3. Select the column to calculate savings on for this custom strategy.
cases.expected: The custom reference is added alongside the defaults with the selected column.
cases.oracle: The custom reference name appears in the Savings panel with its chosen column.

cases.section: How to set Savings references in an Event?
cases.title: Bulk-enter savings references with "Paste from CSV"
cases.why: Large events need bulk entry of reference values.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement manager creating an event with several line items; reference values in an Excel sheet.
cases.steps: 1. Copy the values from Excel. 2. Go to the saving panel. 3. Click "Paste from CSV".
cases.expected: The values are pasted in the cells automatically.
cases.oracle: Each reference cell holds the corresponding copied value.

cases.section: How to add Terms and Conditions for my Vendors in my Events?
cases.title: Remove a T&C with the cross next to it
cases.why: Buyers must be able to correct wrongly attached terms before publishing.
cases.setup: Buyer with the T&C panel open and at least two T&Cs added.
cases.steps: 1. Click the cross next to one T&C. 2. Click **Done**.
cases.expected: The removed term no longer appears; the remaining terms stay.
cases.oracle: Reopened panel lists only the remaining T&Cs.

cases.section: How do I Schedule Events and change Event Duration?
cases.title: Custom end-time duration in Minutes, Hours or Days
cases.why: Non-preset durations are common for real events.
cases.setup: Planner / Buyer / Procurement manager with the Schedule side panel open.
cases.steps: 1. Under End Time, click **Custom Duration**. 2. In the dialog box enter a numeric value and choose the unit (Minutes, Hours, Days). 3. Click **Save**.
cases.expected: The custom duration is confirmed as the event's end-time duration.
cases.oracle: End time equals start + the entered value in the chosen unit.

cases.section: How do I Schedule Events and change Event Duration?
cases.title: Fixed Time end instead of a duration
cases.why: Some events must close at an exact date and time.
cases.setup: Planner / Buyer / Procurement manager with the Schedule side panel open.
cases.steps: 1. Under End Time, change the drop-down from **Duration** to **Fixed Time**. 2. Use the date picker to choose the exact end date and time.
cases.expected: The event is set to end at the chosen date and time.
cases.oracle: The schedule label shows the chosen end date and time.

cases.section: How do I Schedule Events and change Event Duration?
cases.title: Evaluation Time duration (preset or custom)
cases.why: Evaluation time controls how long the event remains open for evaluation after it ends.
cases.setup: Planner / Buyer / Procurement manager with the Schedule side panel open.
cases.steps: 1. Under Evaluation Time, open the drop-down named "Duration". 2. Choose a preset (30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours, 1 day), or choose Custom Duration, enter a numeric value and unit (Minutes, Hours, Days) and click **Save**.
cases.expected: The event remains open for evaluation for the chosen duration after it ends.
cases.oracle: Evaluation Time shows the chosen value; after the end time, evaluation stays available for that duration.

cases.section: How do I Schedule Events and change Event Duration?
cases.title: Evaluation Time "Not Applicable" keeps the evaluation window open indefinitely
cases.why: Stated behaviour: no expiry on evaluation.
cases.setup: Planner / Buyer / Procurement manager with the Schedule side panel open.
cases.steps: 1. Under Evaluation Time, choose **Not Applicable**. 2. Publish the event and let it pass its end time.
cases.expected: The evaluation window stays open indefinitely (no expiry).
cases.oracle: Evaluation remains available long after the event end time.

cases.section: How do I add additional columns to a Template?
cases.title: An added column disappears from its dropdown list
cases.why: Prevents adding the same column twice.
cases.setup: Buyer / Purchaser on the RFQ Event Creation page.
cases.steps: 1. Add a column (e.g. Tick Size) via "+Add Columns" › Creator. 2. Open "+Add Columns" › Creator again.
cases.expected: The dropdown value disappears from its respective list after being added.
cases.oracle: The added column's name is no longer in the list.

cases.section: How do I fill my tempate by uploading an Excel Sheet?
cases.title: "Download template" gives a sheet that opens in Google Sheets or Excel
cases.why: The downloadable template is the contract for the upload format.
cases.setup: Buyer on the RFQ Event Creation page.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Upload Sheet". 2. Click "Download template" in the pop-up. 3. Open the downloaded file in Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel.
cases.expected: A template sheet for filling in line item details is downloaded and opens in either application.
cases.oracle: A downloaded file exists and opens with line-item columns.

cases.section: How do you run an RFQ Event?
cases.title: Review previous bid revisions of a vendor
cases.why: Buyers need bid history to judge negotiation progress.
cases.setup: Buyer; a published RFQ where a vendor has revised a bid at least once.
cases.steps: 1. Hover over the "Current bid" value and select an earlier bid version. 2. Use the arrow buttons next to the bid value to cycle through revisions and back to the current bid.
cases.expected: The vendor's past bids are shown; the buyer can jump to a chosen version and cycle back to the current bid.
cases.oracle: Displayed bid value changes to the selected revision and returns to the current bid.

cases.section: How do you run an RFQ Event?
cases.title: Actions › Enable English Auction converts the RFQ into an English Auction
cases.why: Alternate path that changes the event's bidding mechanics.
cases.setup: Buyer; a published RFQ.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **Actions** button. 2. Select **Enable English Auction**.
cases.expected: The RFQ is converted into an English Auction event.
cases.oracle: The event shows as an English Auction (the article defers details to another page — tester verifies at that level).

cases.section: How do I use Request for Best Offer?
cases.title: Best Offer duration can be set in minutes, hours or days
cases.why: The submission window length is the vendors' deadline to revise.
cases.setup: Buyer / Procurement Manager with the Request for Best Offer panel open.
cases.steps: 1. Enter a duration in minutes and review. 2. Change to hours, then to days.
cases.expected: The duration can be set in minutes, hours, or days.
cases.oracle: Each unit is accepted and the resulting window matches the entered value.

cases.section: How Vendors Review and Update Charges After Lot Splitting
cases.title: "Bid Adjustment Pending" tag and View Item Distribution show the lot restructure
cases.why: The vendor must be told their existing charges may no longer be valid.
cases.setup: Vendor in an RFQ that has been split into lots.
cases.steps: 1. Open the **Live Events** tab. 2. Open the Lot RFQ and click **View Item Distribution**.
cases.expected: The event card carries a **"Bid Adjustment Pending"** tag; View Item Distribution shows how the original line items were reassigned into lots.
cases.oracle: Tag visible on the card; distribution matches the buyer's lot configuration.

cases.section: How Vendors Review and Update Charges After Lot Splitting
cases.title: Vendor review workflow may not apply when the buyer skipped review
cases.why: Stated condition linking the vendor flow to the buyer's skip option.
cases.setup: An RFQ split into lots where the buyer used "Skip Vendor Review" for a vendor.
cases.steps: 1. As that vendor, open the **Live Events** tab and the Lot RFQ.
cases.expected: The review-and-update workflow may not apply for that vendor.
cases.oracle: Tester records whether the "Bid Adjustment Pending" tag and banner are shown (the article says only that the workflow "may not apply").

cases.section: How do I convert an RFQ to an Auction
cases.title: Conversion summary shows vendors who quoted; View All RFQs returns to the RFQ
cases.why: Buyer needs RFQ context while configuring the auction.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Setup screen reached via Convert to Auction; RFQ had several quoting vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Read the summary of how many vendors submitted quotes in the RFQ. 2. Click **View All RFQs**.
cases.expected: The summary shows the number of vendors who submitted quotes; View All RFQs returns to the RFQ to review existing bids.
cases.oracle: Summary count equals the RFQ's quoting vendors; the RFQ bids view opens.

cases.section: How do I convert an RFQ to an Auction
cases.title: Optional auction features during conversion: cost breakdown, dynamic vendor selection, line-wise or lot-wise bidding
cases.why: Alternate configurations available on the converted auction.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Setup screen reached via Convert to Auction.
cases.steps: 1. Enable cost breakdown mode. 2. Enable dynamic vendor selection. 3. Choose line-wise, then lot-wise bidding. 4. **Save** and **Publish**.
cases.expected: Each optional feature can be enabled and the chosen bidding mode is applied to the auction.
cases.oracle: Published auction reflects the selected options (details of each feature are in other articles).

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Default event type for an auction is Rank on Line
cases.why: The default strategy decides what vendors see; a wrong default silently changes auction behaviour.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Create Event screen.
cases.steps: 1. On the **Create Event** screen select **Auction** as the event type. 2. Look at the **Event Type** badge without changing anything.
cases.expected: The Event Type is set to **Rank on Line**, a type of Reverse Auction, by default.
cases.oracle: The Event Type badge reads "Rank on Line".

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Rank on Line badge opens the strategy side drawer
cases.why: The badge is the only stated way to reach the other auction strategies.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Create Event screen with Auction selected.
cases.steps: 1. Click on the **Rank on Line** badge.
cases.expected: A side drawer opens with multiple strategy options.
cases.oracle: The side drawer is visible and lists several auction strategies.

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Auction strategy can be changed before publishing
cases.why: Buyers must be able to correct the strategy while the event is still a draft.
cases.setup: Buyer with an unpublished auction event on the Create Event screen.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **Rank on Line** badge to open the strategy side drawer. 2. Select a different strategy.
cases.expected: The strategy is updated on the unpublished event.
cases.oracle: The Event Type badge shows the newly selected strategy.

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Partial award option runs the auction at line-item level
cases.why: The awarding type decides whether the auction competes per line item or per lot.
cases.setup: Buyer creating an auction event.
cases.steps: 1. Under "Choose how you will award (to the vendors) in the event", pick "I may partially award the event to multiple vendors". 2. Complete and publish the event.
cases.expected: The auction runs at a line item level.
cases.oracle: Bidding and ranks in the live auction are per line item.

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Entire-lot award option runs the auction at lot level
cases.why: Lot-level auctions are required when one vendor must win everything.
cases.setup: Buyer creating an auction event.
cases.steps: 1. Under "Choose how you will award (to the vendors) in the event", pick "I'll award the entire lot to a single vendor". 2. Complete and publish the event.
cases.expected: The auction runs at a Lot Level.
cases.oracle: Bidding and ranks in the live auction are on the lot as a whole.

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: A new product row is added automatically after each product
cases.why: Buyers rely on the auto-added row to enter multiple products quickly.
cases.setup: Buyer creating an auction event with a template selected.
cases.steps: 1. Click the cell beneath the "Products" column and select a product from the dropdown (typing narrows the search).
cases.expected: A new row is automatically added for the next product.
cases.oracle: The template table shows an extra empty row after the product is selected.

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Suggested vendors are added via Invite Vendors
cases.why: Vendor suggestions from product mapping are the fastest way to invite participants.
cases.setup: Buyer creating an auction event; products added have mapped vendors.
cases.steps: 1. After adding products, locate the green tip. 2. Click the blue "Invite Vendors".
cases.expected: The vendors mapped to the added products are automatically added as participants.
cases.oracle: The suggested vendors appear in the event's participants.

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Vendors can be searched, filtered and added manually via Participants
cases.why: Buyers need to invite vendors beyond the automatic suggestions.
cases.setup: Buyer creating an auction event.
cases.steps: 1. Click on Participants. 2. Search or filter vendors and add one manually.
cases.expected: The participants screen opens and the chosen vendor is added.
cases.oracle: The manually added vendor is listed as a participant.

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Event title is auto-generated and editable
cases.why: The auto title must reflect the content yet stay editable for buyer naming conventions.
cases.setup: Buyer creating an auction event with products and a location filled in.
cases.steps: 1. Look at the event title after adding products and location. 2. Edit the title.
cases.expected: Procol auto-generates the title from product and location names, and the buyer can edit it.
cases.oracle: The title initially contains the product and location names and then shows the edited text.

cases.section: How to set up a Reverse Auction?
cases.title: Schedule the auction for later with Edit Schedule
cases.why: Buyers often need the auction to go live at a planned time rather than immediately.
cases.setup: Buyer with a fully filled auction event.
cases.steps: 1. Click the blue "Publish Event" button. 2. In the pop-up, press "Edit Schedule" instead of "Publish".
cases.expected: The event can be scheduled for later instead of going live immediately.
cases.oracle: A tester confirms the event is scheduled rather than immediately live (the article does not name the resulting status).

cases.section: How to choose and configure Auction Strategies?
cases.title: Traffic Light: group vendors by Price or by Rank
cases.why: The grouping condition decides which bands apply.
cases.setup: Buyer creating a Traffic Light auction.
cases.steps: 1. Set the grouping condition to Price, then to Rank.
cases.expected: Either Price or Rank can be selected, and the bands switch to Price-based or Rank-based accordingly.
cases.oracle: The band inputs change between price values and rank values.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Reach the auction from a project's Auction tab
cases.why: Project-based sourcing needs a second entry point to the same auction.
cases.setup: Buyer with a project that contains a published auction.
cases.steps: 1. Go to the project. 2. Navigate to the Auction Tab.
cases.expected: The auction responses for that project are shown.
cases.oracle: The Auction tab shows the vendor quotes for the project's auction.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Savings percentage icon versus the vendor's previous bid
cases.why: Buyers track how much each revision saved.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Responses tab; a vendor has revised a bid.
cases.steps: 1. Look at the revised bid in the comparison.
cases.expected: A percentage icon next to the bid shows the savings compared to that vendor's previous bid.
cases.oracle: The percentage matches the difference between the previous and current bid.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Jump to a previous bid version from the Current bid hover
cases.why: Bid history supports audit and negotiation.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Responses tab; a vendor has revised several times.
cases.steps: 1. Hover over the "Current bid" value. 2. Select a previous bid version.
cases.expected: The vendor's past bids are shown and the buyer can jump to the selected version.
cases.oracle: The displayed bid changes to the chosen past version.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Cycle bid revisions with the arrow buttons
cases.why: Quick stepping through revisions without leaving the QCS.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Auction Responses tab; a vendor has revised several times.
cases.steps: 1. Use the arrow buttons next to the bid value to go back through revisions. 2. Use them to return to the current bid.
cases.expected: The buyer can cycle through previous revisions and go back to the current bid.
cases.oracle: The bid value changes per click and finally shows the current bid again.

cases.section: How to run a Rank-Based Auction event?
cases.title: Disable View-Only Mode by clicking the same action again
cases.why: The mode must be reversible or the buyer loses control of the auction.
cases.setup: Buyer with View-Only Mode enabled on a live auction.
cases.steps: 1. Click **Actions** and click the View-Only Mode action again. 2. Try to send a counter offer.
cases.expected: View-Only Mode is disabled and the restricted actions are available again.
cases.oracle: The counter offer action works after disabling.

cases.title: Vendor sees the total-lot bidding message
cases.why: Vendors must know they are bidding on the lot and will owe a breakdown later.
cases.setup: Vendor invited to a live cost-breakdown auction.
cases.steps: 1. As vendor, open the auction.
cases.expected: The vendor sees "You are bidding on the total lot amount we received from your RFQ Quotes. A request for line item-wise cost breakdown will be triggered once the auction submission time ends."
cases.oracle: The message text is shown on the vendor screen.

cases.title: Buyer extends the Cost Breakdown Time
cases.why: Vendors may need more time to justify prices.
cases.setup: Buyer on a cost-breakdown auction during CBD time.
cases.steps: 1. Extend the Cost Breakdown Time.
cases.expected: The Cost Breakdown Time is extended.
cases.oracle: The CBD end time/timer shows the added time.

cases.title: Breakdown is pre-filled pro rata and editable by the vendor
cases.why: Pre-fill speeds up submission while allowing the vendor to justify item prices.
cases.setup: Vendor during CBD time.
cases.steps: 1. Open the cost breakdown prompt. 2. Change the discount on one price and manually edit another price.
cases.expected: The system has already filled in the auto breakdown (pro-rata discounts); the vendor can change discounts and edit each price.
cases.oracle: Pre-filled values are present initially and the edits are accepted.

cases.section: How to create Serial Bidding events
cases.title: Buyer sees a normal auction interface for serial bidding
cases.why: Serial bidding only changes the vendor experience; the buyer view should stay familiar.
cases.setup: Buyer on a live serial bidding auction.
cases.steps: 1. Open the auction as buyer.
cases.expected: The buyer sees the auction interface similar to a normal auction.
cases.oracle: A tester compares the buyer screen with a normal auction screen.

cases.section: How to Run a Price - Based Auction
cases.title: Turn on Show Rank in a Price Based auction
cases.why: Buyers can add rank visibility on top of best price.
cases.setup: Buyer on a live Price Based auction.
cases.steps: 1. Click on Actions. 2. Click the checkbox next to show Rank to toggle it on.
cases.expected: Ranks are shown next to the Best Price.
cases.oracle: Ranks appear beside the Best Price.

cases.section: How to Run a Traffic Light Auction
cases.title: Best price and rank can also be shown in a Traffic Light auction
cases.why: Buyers can add more visibility to a traffic light auction.
cases.setup: Buyer on a Traffic Light auction.
cases.steps: 1. Look for the options to show Best price and Rank and enable them.
cases.expected: Best price and Rank can be shown in the traffic light auction.
cases.oracle: A tester confirms best price and rank become visible (the article does not name the exact control).

cases.section: How to Run a Knockout Auction
cases.title: Buyer extends the ongoing Knockout round
cases.why: Buyers need to give vendors more time within a round.
cases.setup: Buyer on a live Knockout auction.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **plus button (+)** in the round controls. 2. Select additional time.
cases.expected: The time for the ongoing round is extended.
cases.oracle: The round timer shows the added time.

cases.section: How to Run a Knockout Auction
cases.title: Buyer updates tick size and time difference mid-auction
cases.why: Buyers can change the pace of the knockout while it runs.
cases.setup: Buyer on a live Knockout auction.
cases.steps: 1. Edit the tick size and time difference fields. 2. Click **Update**.
cases.expected: The new tick size and time difference are applied.
cases.oracle: Round details and upcoming offers reflect the updated values.

cases.section: How to Run a Dutch Auction.
cases.title: Buyer extends the ongoing Dutch round
cases.why: Buyers need to give vendors more time within a round.
cases.setup: Buyer on a live Dutch auction.
cases.steps: 1. Click the **plus button (+)** in the round controls. 2. Select additional time.
cases.expected: The time for the ongoing round is extended.
cases.oracle: The round timer shows the added time.

cases.section: How to Run a Dutch Auction.
cases.title: Buyer updates tick size and time difference in a Dutch auction
cases.why: Buyers can change the pace of the Dutch ladder while it runs.
cases.setup: Buyer on a live Dutch auction.
cases.steps: 1. Edit the tick size and time difference fields. 2. Click **Update**.
cases.expected: The new tick size and time difference are applied.
cases.oracle: Round details and upcoming offers reflect the updated values.

cases.section: How to setup a Technical Stage Event?
cases.title: Select a Vendor Assessment template
cases.why: The vendor assessment collects vendor-level technical information in the stage.
cases.setup: Buyer on the Technical Stage of a sourcing event being created.
cases.steps: 1. Click on select template under the "Vendor Assessment" section. 2. Choose a template.
cases.expected: The chosen template is set for the Vendor Assessment section.
cases.oracle: The Vendor Assessment section shows the selected template.

cases.section: How to setup a Technical Stage Event?
cases.title: Evaluators can rank T1/T2/T3 or TA/TNA
cases.why: The rank types define what the buyer later sees as technical outcome.
cases.setup: Technical evaluator assigned on a technical stage with vendor responses.
cases.steps: 1. As the evaluator, open a line item's evaluation. 2. Review the available rank options.
cases.expected: The evaluator can assign ranks (T1, T2, T3) or (TA - Technically Accepted or TNA - Technically Not Accepted).
cases.oracle: The rank options offered match these values.

cases.section: How to run a Technical Stage Event?
cases.title: Technical Stage screen updates as vendors place bids
cases.why: Buyers track vendor technical submissions from this screen.
cases.setup: Buyer with a published RFX event that has a Technical Stage.
cases.steps: 1. Open the Technical Stage Tab before vendors bid. 2. Have a vendor place a bid and reopen the tab.
cases.expected: Once vendors place their bids, the screen shows their submissions.
cases.oracle: The vendor's submission appears on the Technical Stage tab.

cases.section: How to run a Technical Stage Event?
cases.title: Buyer increases the Evaluation time
cases.why: Evaluators may need more time than first allowed.
cases.setup: Buyer on a technical stage after Send to Evaluation.
cases.steps: 1. Increase the Evaluation time.
cases.expected: The Evaluation time is increased.
cases.oracle: A tester confirms the evaluation end time moved (the article does not name the control).

cases.section: How do I Evaluate a Technical Stage?
cases.title: Binary evaluation: Technically Accepted / Technically Not Accepted
cases.why: Binary acceptance is one of the two ranking modes.
cases.setup: Technical Evaluator on a technical stage using binary evaluation.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Add Evaluation" on a line item. 2. Choose Technically Accepted (TA) or Technically Not Accepted (DNA), add a remark and click "OK".
cases.expected: The chosen binary rank is saved on the line item.
cases.oracle: The line item shows TA or DNA.

cases.section: How do I Evaluate a Technical Stage?
cases.title: Ranked evaluation: T1, T2, T3
cases.why: Ranked evaluation orders vendors technically.
cases.setup: Technical Evaluator on a technical stage using ranked evaluation.
cases.steps: 1. Click "Add Evaluation" on a line item. 2. Assign a technical rank such as T1, T2 or T3, add a remark and click "OK".
cases.expected: The rank is saved on the line item.
cases.oracle: The line item shows the assigned T-rank.

cases.section: How do I Evaluate a Technical Stage?
cases.title: Evaluation level follows the buyer's setting (line item or lot)
cases.why: Evaluators must evaluate at the level the buyer chose.
cases.setup: Two events: one set by the buyer to line item level, one to lot level.
cases.steps: 1. As evaluator, click "Add Evaluation" in each event.
cases.expected: Evaluation is at line item level or lot level (entire vendor), as set by the buyer.
cases.oracle: The line-item event asks for a rank per line item; the lot event asks for one per vendor.

cases.section: How do I Evaluate a Technical Stage?
cases.title: Vendor specification changes are highlighted in yellow in the QCS
cases.why: Evaluators must spot vendor deviations from spec.
cases.setup: Technical stage where a vendor changed a specification in their submission.
cases.steps: 1. As evaluator, open the Technical Stage and view the QCS.
cases.expected: Changes made by the vendor are highlighted in yellow in the QCS.
cases.oracle: The changed specification cells are yellow.

cases.section: How do I Evaluate a Technical Stage?
cases.title: Regretted line items are clearly marked
cases.why: Evaluators need to know which items the vendor will not supply.
cases.setup: Technical stage where a vendor regretted a line item.
cases.steps: 1. As evaluator, open the Technical Stage and view that vendor's submission.
cases.expected: Regretted line items are clearly marked, indicating the vendor will not supply them.
cases.oracle: The regretted line item carries a visible regret marker.

cases.section: How do I Evaluate a Technical Stage?
cases.title: After submission the evaluator only watches approval progress
cases.why: The evaluator's part ends at submission until approval completes.
cases.setup: Technical Evaluator who has submitted scores.
cases.steps: 1. Look at the Approval Page after submitting.
cases.expected: The workflow progress is displayed and no further action is required from the evaluator until approval is completed.
cases.oracle: The Approval Page shows progress with no pending action for the evaluator.

cases.section: How do I approve a TR (Technical Recommendation)?
cases.title: TR proposal page shows status, reference, ranks, stages, comments and specification
cases.why: Approvers need the full context to approve correctly.
cases.setup: Approver with a TR pending on them.
cases.steps: 1. Open the TR proposal from "Pending on Me" via the arrow icon.
cases.expected: The page shows TR Status, Project Reference ID, Technical Ranks, Approval Workflow Stages, Comments (from earlier approvers or the technical evaluator) and Technical Specification.
cases.oracle: All six items are visible on the proposal page.

cases.section: How do I approve a TR (Technical Recommendation)?
cases.title: "Pending on Me" lists approvals awaiting the user
cases.why: Approvers find their work from this list.
cases.setup: Approver with at least one TR pending on them.
cases.steps: 1. Open the **Approvals** tab and click **"Pending on Me"**.
cases.expected: All approvals awaiting the user's action are listed.
cases.oracle: The pending TR appears in the list.

cases.section: How do I Request for Revaluation?
cases.title: Select all or specific line items for re-evaluation
cases.why: Buyers may dispute the whole evaluation or just part of it.
cases.setup: Buyer with the "Request Re-Evaluation" drawer open; several eligible line items.
cases.steps: 1. Select all eligible line items and send the request. 2. On another event, select only specific items and send.
cases.expected: Both all and specific selections are accepted, and only the selected items are marked.
cases.oracle: Exactly the selected items show "Re-evaluation Requested."

cases.section: How do Re-Evaluate Line items in Technical Stage?
cases.title: Re-evaluation request shows reason, requester and original scores
cases.why: Evaluators need the context to decide whether to accept.
cases.setup: Technical Evaluator on an event with a re-evaluation request.
cases.steps: 1. Open a "Re-evaluation Requested" line item.
cases.expected: The reason, the buyer who raised the request, and the original technical scores and recommendations are visible.
cases.oracle: All three are shown on the request.

cases.section: How do Re-Evaluate Line items in Technical Stage?
cases.title: Approval flow selection on re-evaluation submit when workflows are enabled
cases.why: Revised ranks must go through approval again where workflows apply.
cases.setup: Technical Evaluator who accepted a re-evaluation on an org with approval workflows enabled.
cases.steps: 1. After modifying scores, click Submit under the TR status widget. 2. Add closing remarks and select the approval flow. 3. Click **Submit**.
cases.expected: The appropriate approval flow is selected for the updated evaluation.
cases.oracle: The submission shows the chosen approval flow.

cases.section: Surrogate Bidding: How to Place Bids on Behalf of Vendors
cases.title: Surrogate bid placed in a Technical Stage
cases.why: The article states surrogate bids can be placed in a technical evaluation, not only commercial stages; the technical stage form differs and must accept a buyer-entered response.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. An event with a Technical Stage and a participating vendor who has not responded.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the project details page for the event. 2. Go to the Technical Stage tab. 3. Click on the Participants section and locate the vendor. 4. Click "➕ Add Bid" next to the vendor's name. 5. Enter the vendor's response in the bid form, attach a Surrogate Bid Reference and click Submit.
cases.expected: The surrogate response is recorded against the vendor in the Technical Stage.
cases.oracle: The Technical Stage comparison (QCS) shows the vendor's response marked "Surrogate Bid" under the vendor's name.

cases.section: Surrogate Bidding: How to Place Bids on Behalf of Vendors
cases.title: Surrogate bid placed in a Reverse Auction stage
cases.why: Reverse Auction is one of the three stage tabs the article names for surrogate bidding; auction bids drive ranking live, so a surrogate bid must be accepted there too.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. An event with a live Reverse Auction stage and a participating vendor.
cases.steps: 1. Navigate to the project details page for the event. 2. Go to the Reverse Auction tab. 3. Click on the Participants section and locate the vendor. 4. Click "➕ Add Bid" next to the vendor's name. 5. Enter the vendor's bid, attach a Surrogate Bid Reference and click Submit.
cases.expected: The surrogate bid is recorded for the vendor in the Reverse Auction stage.
cases.oracle: The auction QCS shows the vendor's bid marked "Surrogate Bid" under the vendor's name in blue text next to the currency.

cases.section: Surrogate Bidding: How to Place Bids on Behalf of Vendors
cases.title: Participants section lists vendor details and supports search
cases.why: The buyer must pick the right vendor before entering an offline bid; the article says the list shows identifying details and a search bar.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. An event stage (Technical Stage, RFQ or Reverse Auction) with several participating vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Open the event's project details page and the relevant stage tab. 2. Click on the Participants section. 3. Type a vendor's name into the search bar.
cases.expected: The vendor list shows name, phone number, email and vendor code, and the search narrows the list to the matching vendor with its "➕ Add Bid" button.
cases.oracle: Participants list columns show name, phone number, email and vendor code; after searching only the matching vendor row is shown.

cases.section: Surrogate Bidding: How to Place Bids on Behalf of Vendors
cases.title: Surrogate bid form mirrors the vendor form and supports Quick Fill
cases.why: The article states the buyer sees the same form the vendor would fill; a divergent form would let surrogate bids skip required vendor fields. Quick Fill is the stated speed-up for many similar entries.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. An RFQ event with several line items and a participating vendor.
cases.steps: 1. Open the Participants section of the RFQ stage and click "➕ Add Bid" next to the vendor. 2. Compare the fields with the vendor's own bid form for the same event. 3. Use Quick Fill to copy-paste or autofill values across similar entries.
cases.expected: The surrogate form has the same fields as the vendor's form, and Quick Fill populates the applicable fields.
cases.oracle: Field-by-field comparison with the vendor's form matches; fields targeted by Quick Fill show the filled values before Submit.

cases.section: Surrogate Bidding: How to Place Bids on Behalf of Vendors
cases.title: Supplier Remarks and Surrogate Bid Reference are saved with the surrogate bid
cases.why: The reference attachment (screenshots, call logs, emails) is the audit evidence that the vendor really offered this bid; remarks carry vendor conditions such as "Final price, no further negotiation."
cases.setup: Buyer persona. An RFQ event and an offline record file of the vendor's bid.
cases.steps: 1. Open "➕ Add Bid" for the vendor from the Participants section. 2. Enter the bid values. 3. Add Supplier Remarks, e.g. "Final price, no further negotiation." 4. Attach a Surrogate Bid Reference file. 5. Click Submit. 6. Reopen the vendor's bid details.
cases.expected: The remark and the attached reference are kept with the surrogate bid.
cases.oracle: The vendor's bid details show the remark text and the attached reference file.

cases.section: How to Send and Manage Counter Offers?
cases.title: Counter offer dialog shows original vendor value next to the counter value
cases.why: The buyer must see what they are countering against to avoid sending a wrong value.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. RFQ event with a vendor bid in the QCS.
cases.steps: 1. Open the QCS on the RFQ tab. 2. Click **"Counter Offer"** beneath a vendor's name. 3. Select the Price field and input a new value.
cases.expected: The dialog shows both the original vendor value and the counter offer value for comparison.
cases.oracle: In the dialog the vendor's original value and the entered counter offer value are displayed side by side.

cases.section: How to Send and Manage Counter Offers?
cases.title: Counter offer on a Global Field
cases.why: The article states counter offers can also be sent on Global Fields (fields not specific to any line item), e.g. event-level terms.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. RFQ event with at least one global field and a vendor bid in the QCS.
cases.steps: 1. Open the QCS on the RFQ tab and click **"Counter Offer"** beneath the vendor's name. 2. Select a global field in the dialog. 3. Input the new value and click **"Send Counter Offer"**.
cases.expected: The counter offer on the global field is sent.
cases.oracle: Success tooltip; "Counter Offer Requested" tag above the vendor's name; the global field value is highlighted with original vs counter value.

cases.section: How to Send and Manage Counter Offers?
cases.title: Counter offer can be sent without the optional note
cases.why: The note to the vendor is stated as helpful but not mandatory; the form must not block sending when it is empty.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. RFQ event with a vendor bid in the QCS.
cases.steps: 1. Open **"Counter Offer"** for a vendor. 2. Select Price and input a new value. 3. Leave the note to the vendor empty. 4. Click **"Send Counter Offer"**.
cases.expected: The counter offer is sent without a note.
cases.oracle: Success tooltip appears and the "Counter Offer Requested" tag shows above the vendor's name.

cases.section: How to Send Bulk Counter Offers?
cases.title: Bulk counter offer on a Global Field
cases.why: The article states bulk counter offers can also target Global Fields not tied to a line item.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. RFQ event with a global field and several vendor bids.
cases.steps: 1. Click on Settings and choose "Send Bulk Counter Offers". 2. Select a global field and input the new value. 3. Click **"Send Counter Offer"**.
cases.expected: The global-field counter offer is sent to all vendors.
cases.oracle: Success tooltip; "Counter Offer Requested" tag above every vendor's name; global field value highlighted original vs counter.

cases.section: How to Send Bulk Counter Offers?
cases.title: Bulk counter offer sent without the optional note
cases.why: The note is optional in the bulk flow too; sending must not require it.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. RFQ event with several vendor bids.
cases.steps: 1. Click on Settings and choose "Send Bulk Counter Offers". 2. Select Price and input a new value; leave the note empty. 3. Click **"Send Counter Offer"**.
cases.expected: The bulk counter offer is sent without a note.
cases.oracle: Success tooltip and "Counter Offer Requested" tag above every vendor's name.

cases.section: How to Send Bulk Counter Offers?
cases.title: Revoke option and highlighted values appear after a bulk counter offer
cases.why: After a bulk send the buyer still needs per-vendor control and a visible diff of what was countered.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. A bulk counter offer has just been sent on an RFQ event.
cases.steps: 1. Open the QCS after sending the bulk counter offer. 2. Inspect each vendor's header and the countered field.
cases.expected: Each vendor shows the pending counter offer with a revoke option and highlighted changes.
cases.oracle: "Revoke Counter Offer" option is shown for the vendors; changed values are highlighted showing original vs counter offer values.

cases.section: How do I Modify Counter Offers as a Vendor?
cases.title: Choosing Modify Counter Offer changes the banner and exposes an editable field
cases.why: After choosing modify the vendor needs an editable value to enter the re-counter; the article states the banner changes.
cases.setup: Vendor persona. RFQ event with a pending counter offer.
cases.steps: 1. Click the counter offer Decline option. 2. Choose **"Modify Counter Offer"**.
cases.expected: The banner changes and an editable field for the updated value is available, with the "Place Modified Bid" button.
cases.oracle: The banner content differs from the original Counter Offer Banner; an editable value field and a blue "Place Modified Bid" button are visible.

cases.section: How do I Modify Counter Offers as a Vendor?
cases.title: Vendor's modification remark reaches the buyer
cases.why: The article says the remark helps buyers understand the pricing rationale; if it is dropped the buyer sees an unexplained price.
cases.setup: Vendor and Buyer personas. RFQ event with a pending counter offer.
cases.steps: 1. As the vendor, choose **"Modify Counter Offer"**, enter an updated value and add a remark explaining the modification. 2. Click **"Place Modified Bid"**. 3. As the buyer, open the QCS and view the vendor's modified bid.
cases.expected: The buyer can read the vendor's remark alongside the modified value.
cases.oracle: Buyer's QCS shows the "Modified Counter Offer Bid" tag and the vendor's remark text for that bid.

cases.section: How to Award Vendors and Submit Proposal for Approval
cases.title: Global charges comparison across commercial stages at the bottom of the awarding screen
cases.why: The article's note says global charges and other costs can be compared between commercial stages before awarding.
cases.setup: Buyer persona. Event with more than one commercial stage and global charges; awarding screen open.
cases.steps: 1. On the awarding screen, scroll to the bottom.
cases.expected: Global charges and other costs are shown for comparison between the commercial stages.
cases.oracle: The bottom section of the awarding screen lists global charges/costs per commercial stage.

cases.title: View by Vendor shows a quote card per vendor
cases.why: Vendor mode lets evaluators review each quote in isolation instead of the comparative table.
cases.setup: Buyer, Technical Evaluator or Category Manager; an event with quotes from several vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Open the QCS. 2. Click **View by Product** to open the dropdown with **Vendor** and Product. 3. Click on Vendor.
cases.expected: The QCS shows a vendor-specific quote breakdown with a dedicated quote card for each vendor instead of the comparative table.
cases.oracle: One quote card per vendor is displayed; the comparative table is not shown.

cases.title: Hide Fields removes chosen columns from the QCS
cases.why: Hiding irrelevant columns (GST, Quantity, Delivery Terms) focuses evaluation on relevant fields; hidden columns must actually disappear.
cases.setup: Buyer, Technical Evaluator or Category Manager; an event whose QCS has GST, Quantity and Delivery Terms columns.
cases.steps: 1. Open the QCS. 2. Use the **Hide Fields** option. 3. Hide GST, Quantity and Delivery Terms.
cases.expected: The chosen columns are hidden from the QCS.
cases.oracle: GST, Quantity and Delivery Terms columns are no longer shown; other columns remain.

cases.title: Vendor Masking on a live Auction event
cases.why: The article states masking is available on the Auction Event screen as well as RFQ.
cases.setup: Buyer on a live Auction event with at least two participating vendors.
cases.steps: 1. Go to the **Auction Event** screen where the event is live. 2. Click the **Actions** button. 3. Select **Enable Vendor Masking**.
cases.expected: Vendor names are replaced with Vendor 1, 2, 3 … N until bidding ends.
cases.oracle: Auction screen shows Vendor 1, Vendor 2, … instead of real names.

cases.section: How to enable Show Best Price?
cases.title: Best price reflects the current lowest bid after a vendor rebids
cases.why: The feature shows the current lowest bid and vendors use it to update bids competitively; a stale best price misleads bidding.
cases.setup: **Show Best Prices** enabled; at least two vendors have bid on a line item.
cases.steps: 1. Note the best price for a line item. 2. As a vendor who is not L1, update the bid below the shown best price. 3. As the buyer, view the best-price row in the QCS; as another vendor, view the best price.
cases.expected: The best price updates to the new lowest bid for both buyer and vendors.
cases.oracle: Best-price row and vendor-side best price both equal the new lower bid.

cases.title: Email Notifications: on failure — failed emails retried 3x

cases.expected: The stated failure handling happens: failed emails retried 3x.
cases.oracle: Evidence of exactly this handling is visible (state, alert, log or retry record as named) and nothing is silently dropped.

cases.section: How to create a Sourcing Project (Technical Stage, RFQ, Auction)?
cases.title: Crossed-out eye marks a stage not yet reviewed
cases.why: Visual cue that the buyer has not reviewed a stage before publishing.

cases.steps: 1. Without opening the Technical Stage, look at its tab. 2. Click on Technical Stage to review it.
cases.expected: A crossed-out eye is shown next to the technical stage until it has been reviewed by the user.
cases.oracle: Icon present before review; tester checks whether it clears after review.

cases.title: Cost Breakdown Mode tooltip text
cases.why: The tooltip is the in-product explanation of the mode.
cases.setup: Buyer on the auction creation page.
cases.steps: 1. Hover over the eye icon beside "Enable Cost Breakdown Mode".
cases.expected: The tooltip reads "Choosing this option will enable vendors to submit their responses with a single value. Vendors will be asked to fill the justified prices in the allotted CBD Time after the bidding ends."
cases.oracle: The tooltip text matches exactly.

cases.title: Switch the QCS between vertical and horizontal view
cases.why: Layout choice affects readability of vendor comparisons; the toggle must switch the layout without losing data.
cases.setup: Buyer, Technical Evaluator or Category Manager reviewing vendor quotations; an event with vendor quotes in the QCS.
cases.steps: 1. Open the QCS. 2. Click the layout toggle button. 3. Click the layout toggle button again.
cases.expected: The QCS switches between vertical and horizontal views.
cases.oracle: The QCS layout changes orientation on each click with the same vendor data shown.

cases.title: Full screen mode expands the QCS
cases.why: Full screen supports deep analysis on large monitors during evaluation meetings.

cases.steps: 1. Open the QCS. 2. Click the **full screen icon**.
cases.expected: The QCS expands across the display.
cases.oracle: The QCS occupies the full display area.

cases.title: Zoom control changes QCS text size

cases.expected: Text size increases on zoom in and decreases on zoom out.
cases.oracle: QCS text renders larger after zoom in and smaller after zoom out.

cases.title: Auto button resizes rows/columns to Small, Medium, Large or XL

cases.expected: Row height / column width changes to the selected size.
cases.oracle: QCS row height or column width visibly changes for each option.

journeys.title: Running a reverse auction
journeys.goal: Select qualified vendors into a reverse auction, set its strategy, caps and time controls, run it live and negotiate after it closes.

cases.title: Vendor Selection into Auction: happy path for the Buyer
cases.why: Focused competition. Business use: Before the auction; the buyer selects which qualified vendors advance.
cases.setup: Persona: Buyer. Plan: tenant on Growth (lowest plan with access; Plan Required: Growth, Enterprise). Status: GA.
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as a Buyer on the tenant described in Setup and open Reverse Auction. 2. Choose which vendors advance to the auction. 3. Follow the business scenario the workbook gives: "Before the auction; the buyer selects which qualified vendors advance". 4. Check the result against the story's promised outcome.
cases.expected: The Buyer achieves the story's outcome: curate the live bidder set. The business use case is served: before the auction; the buyer selects which qualified vendors advance.
cases.oracle: Observable proof that Vendor Selection into Auction did its job for the Buyer — the outcome in Expected is visible in Procol after the last step, with no error, on the plan in Setup. Any gap is a defect against FEAT-RA-001.

journeys.title: Receiving goods: ASN, GRN and quality check
journeys.goal: The vendor announces a shipment (ASN), the warehouse receives it against the PO (GRN), and quality inspects it — pass, fail or partial accept — including MDCC, FAT and PDI.

cases.expected: The user without the role cannot carry out the action — Procol refuses it or does not offer it — while the Quality Manager can. (If the tenant's RBAC deliberately grants it to more roles, record that configuration rather than a defect.)
cases.oracle: Same tenant, same steps, different role: refused or absent for the other user, available to the Quality Manager.

cases.section: Roadmap features — not in the product yet (acceptance specifications)
cases.title: [Roadmap] ASN Discrepancy Alerts: tenant configuration — Alert thresholds should be configurable per category
cases.why: The workbook says "Alert thresholds should be configurable per category". A setting a tenant can change is a gate: the feature must follow whatever the tenant chose, for every allowed choice.
cases.setup: Persona: Tenant Admin (to change the setting) and Buyer / Warehouse Executive (to use the feature). Plan: tenant on Enterprise (lowest plan with access; Plan Required: Enterprise). Status: Roadmap (Suggested — not in product yet) — this is an acceptance specification; run it once the feature ships. The Configuration Reference sheet names no config key for this; the setting is the one the note describes.
cases.steps: 1. As a Tenant Admin, find the tenant setting the note refers to ("Alert thresholds should be configurable per category") and record its current value. 2. As the Buyer / Warehouse Executive: use ASN Discrepancy Alerts to be alerted when ASN and PO details diverge. 3. Change the setting to a different allowed value, then repeat step 2.
cases.expected: In both runs ASN Discrepancy Alerts follows the tenant's configured value, as the workbook states: "Alert thresholds should be configurable per category". Changing the setting changes the behaviour accordingly.
cases.oracle: The behaviour observed in step 2 and step 3 differs exactly as the two configured values dictate; identical behaviour under different settings means the setting is ignored.

cases.section: Roadmap features — not in the product yet (acceptance specifications)
cases.title: [Roadmap] MDCC Rejection & Re-Inspection Cycle: happy path for the Quality Inspector
cases.why: Prevents non-conforming goods from ever being dispatched. Business use: Failed MDCC blocks dispatch clearance and routes to a corrective-action/re-inspection loop.
cases.setup: Persona: Quality Inspector. Plan: tenant on Enterprise (lowest plan with access; Plan Required: Enterprise). Status: Roadmap (Suggested — not in product yet) — this is an acceptance specification; run it once the feature ships.
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as a Quality Inspector on the tenant described in Setup and open Quality Check (incl. MDCC, FAT, PDI). 2. Use MDCC Rejection & Re-Inspection Cycle to get what the story asks for: a failed MDCC inspection to trigger a re-inspection cycle. 3. Follow the business scenario the workbook gives: "Failed MDCC blocks dispatch clearance and routes to a corrective-action/re-inspection loop". 4. Check the result against the story's promised outcome.
cases.expected: The Quality Inspector achieves the story's outcome: dispatch is blocked until issues are resolved. The business use case is served: failed MDCC blocks dispatch clearance and routes to a corrective-action/re-inspection loop.
cases.oracle: Observable proof that MDCC Rejection & Re-Inspection Cycle did its job for the Quality Inspector — the outcome in Expected is visible in Procol after the last step, with no error, on the plan in Setup. Any gap is a defect against FEAT-QC-013.

cases.section: Roadmap features — not in the product yet (acceptance specifications)
cases.title: [Roadmap] MDCC Rejection & Re-Inspection Cycle: tenant configuration — Number of re-inspection cycles allowed should be configurable
cases.why: The workbook says "Number of re-inspection cycles allowed should be configurable". A setting a tenant can change is a gate: the feature must follow whatever the tenant chose, for every allowed choice.
cases.setup: Persona: Tenant Admin (to change the setting) and Quality Inspector (to use the feature). Plan: tenant on Enterprise (lowest plan with access; Plan Required: Enterprise). Status: Roadmap (Suggested — not in product yet) — this is an acceptance specification; run it once the feature ships. The Configuration Reference sheet names no config key for this; the setting is the one the note describes.
cases.steps: 1. As a Tenant Admin, find the tenant setting the note refers to ("Number of re-inspection cycles allowed should be configurable") and record its current value. 2. As the Quality Inspector: use MDCC Rejection & Re-Inspection Cycle to get a failed MDCC inspection to trigger a re-inspection cycle. 3. Change the setting to a different allowed value, then repeat step 2.
cases.expected: In both runs MDCC Rejection & Re-Inspection Cycle follows the tenant's configured value, as the workbook states: "Number of re-inspection cycles allowed should be configurable". Changing the setting changes the behaviour accordingly.
cases.oracle: The behaviour observed in step 2 and step 3 differs exactly as the two configured values dictate; identical behaviour under different settings means the setting is ignored.

cases.setup: Persona: a user who holds none of these roles: Vendor. Plan: tenant on Enterprise (lowest plan with access; Plan Required: Enterprise). Status: GA (Already in Procol).
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as that user on the tenant described in Setup. 2. Try it: use Vendor Self-Service Invoice Submission Portal to submit invoices directly through a portal. 3. Repeat as a Vendor.
cases.expected: The user without the role cannot carry out the action — Procol refuses it or does not offer it — while the Vendor can. (If the tenant's RBAC deliberately grants it to more roles, record that configuration rather than a defect.)
cases.oracle: Same tenant, same steps, different role: refused or absent for the other user, available to the Vendor.

cases.title: Invoice Aging Report: tenant configuration — Aging buckets are configurable per tenant
cases.why: The workbook says "Aging buckets are configurable per tenant". A setting a tenant can change is a gate: the feature must follow whatever the tenant chose, for every allowed choice.
cases.setup: Persona: Tenant Admin (to change the setting) and AP Manager (to use the feature). Plan: tenant on Growth (lowest plan with access; Plan Required: Growth, Enterprise). Status: GA (Already in Procol). The Configuration Reference sheet names no config key for this; the setting is the one the note describes.
cases.steps: 1. As a Tenant Admin, find the tenant setting the note refers to ("Aging buckets are configurable per tenant") and record its current value. 2. As the AP Manager: use Invoice Aging Report to get an invoice aging report by bucket. 3. Change the setting to a different allowed value, then repeat step 2.
cases.expected: In both runs Invoice Aging Report follows the tenant's configured value, as the workbook states: "Aging buckets are configurable per tenant". Changing the setting changes the behaviour accordingly.
cases.oracle: The behaviour observed in step 2 and step 3 differs exactly as the two configured values dictate; identical behaviour under different settings means the setting is ignored.

cases.title: Invoice Aging Report: not available on plans below Growth
cases.why: The workbook limits Invoice Aging Report to "Growth, Enterprise". A tenant on a lower plan must not get it, or plan packaging is not enforced.
cases.setup: Persona: AP Manager. Plan: tenant on a plan below Growth (any plan not listed in "Growth, Enterprise") (Plan Required: Growth, Enterprise). Status: GA (Already in Procol).
cases.steps: 1. Sign in as an AP Manager on the lower-plan tenant. 2. Try it: use Invoice Aging Report to get an invoice aging report by bucket. 3. Repeat on a tenant on Growth.
cases.expected: On a plan below Growth (any plan not listed in "Growth, Enterprise") the capability is not available to use. On Growth the same steps work.
cases.oracle: Same user role, same steps, different plan: refused or absent on the lower plan, available on Growth.

cases.title: Escalation Timeout (Hours) (approval.escalation.timeout_hours) = 48 (default)
cases.why: Without a timeout, approvals can stall indefinitely. SLA-based escalation ensures procurement cycles don't block on individual approver availability.
cases.setup: Persona: Tenant Admin. Plan: any tenant (Plan Required: All Plans). gate: `approval.escalation.timeout_hours` = 48 (default: 48) — CONF-AE-002 "Escalation Timeout (Hours)", Number, risk if changed: Medium.
cases.steps: 1. As the Tenant Admin, set `approval.escalation.timeout_hours` to 48. 2. As a Tenant Admin: use Condition-Based Triggering to get approvals triggered by conditions like value or category. 3. Observe the behaviour the setting controls: number of hours an approval can remain pending before it is auto-escalated to the next level.
cases.expected: The value 48 is accepted and takes effect. What the setting controls: Number of hours an approval can remain pending before it is auto-escalated to the next level. Stated business impact: Setting too low creates approval fatigue; too high defeats the purpose of escalation. Must be aligned to the tenant's internal SLA policy.
cases.oracle: The behaviour in step 3 reflects the value 48 exactly (the boundary of 1 – 720 is honoured).

cases.title: Escalation Timeout (Hours) with DoA Threshold Currency correctly configured (DEP-006)
cases.why: Escalation Timeout (Hours) depends on DoA Threshold Currency. Always configure CONF-AE-001 (DoA Currency) before setting up escalation policies in CONF-AE-002.
cases.setup: Source: CONF-AE-002 "Escalation Timeout (Hours)" (`approval.escalation.timeout_hours`). Depends on: CONF-AE-001 "DoA Threshold Currency" (`approval.doa.currency`) (Conditional). gate: `approval.escalation.timeout_hours`. gate: `approval.doa.currency`. Condition: Only matters when DoA matrix thresholds trigger escalation. Workbook guidance: Always configure CONF-AE-001 (DoA Currency) before setting up escalation policies in CONF-AE-002. DoA Threshold Currency configured correctly.
cases.steps: 1. Configure DoA Threshold Currency (CONF-AE-001) correctly. 2. Configure Escalation Timeout (Hours) (CONF-AE-002). 3. Exercise the behaviour Escalation Timeout (Hours) controls with the condition true (only matters when DoA matrix thresholds trigger escalation).
cases.expected: Escalation Timeout (Hours) works as configured; none of the stated failure impact occurs.
cases.oracle: The impact named in the missing-dependency case (DEP-006) is absent.

Condition: Only matters when DoA matrix thresholds trigger escalation. Workbook guidance: Always configure CONF-AE-001 (DoA Currency) before setting up escalation policies in CONF-AE-002. DoA Threshold Currency missing or misconfigured.
cases.steps: 1. Leave DoA Threshold Currency (CONF-AE-001) missing or misconfigured. 2. Configure Escalation Timeout (Hours) (CONF-AE-002). 3. Exercise the behaviour Escalation Timeout (Hours) controls with the condition true (only matters when DoA matrix thresholds trigger escalation).

cases.oracle: The consequence named in Expected can be observed; if Procol instead prevents the misconfiguration up front, record that as the actual (safer) behaviour.

cases.title: Escalation Timeout (Hours): dependency on DoA Threshold Currency does not apply when "Only matters when DoA matrix thresholds trigger escalation" is false (DEP-006)
cases.why: The dependency is conditional: "Only matters when DoA matrix thresholds trigger escalation". Outside that condition, DoA Threshold Currency must not constrain Escalation Timeout (Hours).
cases.setup: Source: CONF-AE-002 "Escalation Timeout (Hours)" (`approval.escalation.timeout_hours`). cases.steps: 1. Make the condition false. 2. Leave DoA Threshold Currency unconfigured and configure Escalation Timeout (Hours). 3. Exercise the behaviour Escalation Timeout (Hours) controls.
cases.expected: Escalation Timeout (Hours) works without DoA Threshold Currency; the stated impact does not occur.
cases.oracle: No trace of the impact "If DoA currency is misconfigured, amount-based escalation rules may route to…".

cases.title: Budget Creation: tenant configuration — Hierarchy key is fully configurable, not fixed to cost center alone
cases.why: The workbook says "Hierarchy key is fully configurable, not fixed to cost center alone". A setting a tenant can change is a gate: the feature must follow whatever the tenant chose, for every allowed choice.
cases.setup: Persona: Tenant Admin (to change the setting) and Finance Controller (to use the feature). Plan: tenant on Enterprise (lowest plan with access; Plan Required: Enterprise). Status: GA (Already in Procol). The Configuration Reference sheet names no config key for this; the setting is the one the note describes.
cases.steps: 1. As a Tenant Admin, find the tenant setting the note refers to ("Hierarchy key is fully configurable, not fixed to cost center alone") and record its current value. 2. As the Finance Controller: use Budget Creation to create budgets against any configurable hierarchy key. 3. Change the setting to a different allowed value, then repeat step 2.
cases.expected: In both runs Budget Creation follows the tenant's configured value, as the workbook states: "Hierarchy key is fully configurable, not fixed to cost center alone". Changing the setting changes the behaviour accordingly.
cases.oracle: The behaviour observed in step 2 and step 3 differs exactly as the two configured values dictate; identical behaviour under different settings means the setting is ignored.

cases.setup: Persona: Tenant Admin (to change the setting) and Finance Controller (to use the feature). Plan: tenant on Enterprise (lowest plan with access; Plan Required: Enterprise). Status: Roadmap (Suggested — not in product yet) — this is an acceptance specification; run it once the feature ships. The Configuration Reference sheet names no config key for this; the setting is the one the note describes.
cases.steps: 1. As a Tenant Admin, find the tenant setting the note refers to ("Threshold % and recipients configurable per budget line") and record its current value. 2. As the Finance Controller: use Budget Threshold Alerts to get alerts when a budget line crosses a threshold (e.g., 80% consumed). 3. Change the setting to a different allowed value, then repeat step 2.
cases.expected: In both runs Budget Threshold Alerts follows the tenant's configured value, as the workbook states: "Threshold % and recipients configurable per budget line". Changing the setting changes the behaviour accordingly.
cases.oracle: The behaviour observed in step 2 and step 3 differs exactly as the two configured values dictate; identical behaviour under different settings means the setting is ignored.
